# ============================================================================
# VISUALIZATION AND ANALYSIS UTILITIES
# ============================================================================

class CompositionalAnalyzer:
    """Utility class for analyzing compositional generalization patterns."""
    
    def __init__(self, model: nn.Module, model_type: str):
        """
        Args:
            model: Trained compositional model
            model_type: Type of model ('systematic', 'compositional_attn', 
                       'modular', 'symbolic')
        """
        self.model = model
        self.model_type = model_type
        self.model.eval()
    
    def analyze_compositionality(
        self,
        test_loader: DataLoader,
        device: str = 'cpu'
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Analyze compositional properties of the model.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with various analysis metrics
        """
        self.model.to(device)
        analysis_results = {}
        
        if self.model_type == 'systematic':
            analysis_results = self._analyze_systematic(test_loader, device)
        elif self.model_type == 'compositional_attn':
            analysis_results = self._analyze_attention(test_loader, device)
        elif self.model_type == 'modular':
            analysis_results = self._analyze_modular(test_loader, device)
        elif self.model_type == 'symbolic':
            analysis_results = self._analyze_symbolic(test_loader, device)
        
        return analysis_results
    
    def _analyze_systematic(
        self,
        test_loader: DataLoader,
        device: str
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """Analyze systematic generalization model."""
        all_primitives = []
        all_roles = []
        all_bindings = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for data, _ in test_loader:
                data = data.to(device)
                _, aux_outputs = self.model(data)
                
                all_primitives.append(aux_outputs['primitives'].cpu())
                all_roles.append(aux_outputs['roles'].cpu())
                all_bindings.append(aux_outputs['bound'].cpu())
        
        # Concatenate all batches
        primitives = torch.cat(all_primitives, dim=0)  # [N, num_primitives, hidden_dim]
        roles = torch.cat(all_roles, dim=0)  # [N, num_roles, hidden_dim]
        bindings = torch.cat(all_bindings, dim=0)  # [N, num_roles, hidden_dim]
        
        # Compute primitive diversity (average pairwise distance)
        num_samples = primitives.shape[0]
        num_primitives = primitives.shape[1]
        
        primitive_diversity = []
        for i in range(num_primitives):
            prim_i = primitives[:, i, :]  # [N, hidden_dim]
            # Compute pairwise distances
            distances = torch.cdist(prim_i, prim_i, p=2)
            avg_dist = distances.mean().item()
            primitive_diversity.append(avg_dist)
        
        # Compute role consistency (how consistent roles are across samples)
        role_consistency = []
        for i in range(roles.shape[1]):
            role_i = roles[:, i, :]
            # Compute variance
            role_var = role_i.var(dim=0).mean().item()
            role_consistency.append(role_var)
        
        # Compute binding quality (correlation between primitives and bound representations)
        binding_correlations = []
        for sample_idx in range(min(100, num_samples)):
            prims = primitives[sample_idx]  # [num_primitives, hidden_dim]
            bounds = bindings[sample_idx]  # [num_roles, hidden_dim]
            
            # Compute correlation matrix
            prims_norm = F.normalize(prims, p=2, dim=1)
            bounds_norm = F.normalize(bounds, p=2, dim=1)
            corr = torch.mm(prims_norm, bounds_norm.t())
            binding_correlations.append(corr.abs().mean().item())
        
        return {
            'primitive_diversity': np.mean(primitive_diversity),
            'primitive_diversity_std': np.std(primitive_diversity),
            'role_consistency': np.mean(role_consistency),
            'role_consistency_std': np.std(role_consistency),
            'binding_quality': np.mean(binding_correlations),
            'binding_quality_std': np.std(binding_correlations),
            'num_primitives': num_primitives,
            'num_roles': roles.shape[1]
        }
    
    def _analyze_attention(
        self,
        test_loader: DataLoader,
        device: str
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """Analyze compositional attention model."""
        all_level_outputs = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for data, _ in test_loader:
                data = data.to(device)
                _, aux_outputs = self.model(data)
                all_level_outputs.append(aux_outputs['level_outputs'])
        
        # Analyze level diversity
        num_layers = len(all_level_outputs[0])
        num_levels = len(all_level_outputs[0][0])
        
        level_diversity = []
        for layer_idx in range(num_layers):
            layer_diversity = []
            for level_idx in range(num_levels):
                # Collect outputs from this level across batches
                level_outputs = [
                    batch[layer_idx][level_idx]
                    for batch in all_level_outputs
                ]
                level_outputs = torch.cat(level_outputs, dim=0)  # [N, seq_len, embed_dim]
                
                # Compute diversity as variance
                diversity = level_outputs.var(dim=(0, 1)).mean().item()
                layer_diversity.append(diversity)
            
            level_diversity.append(layer_diversity)
        
        return {
            'level_diversity_per_layer': level_diversity,
            'avg_level_diversity': np.mean(level_diversity),
            'num_layers': num_layers,
            'num_levels': num_levels
        }
    
    def _analyze_modular(
        self,
        test_loader: DataLoader,
        device: str
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """Analyze modular compositional model."""
        all_routing_weights = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for data, _ in test_loader:
                data = data.to(device)
                _, aux_outputs = self.model(data)
                all_routing_weights.append(aux_outputs['routing_weights'])
        
        # Analyze module usage
        num_layers = len(all_routing_weights[0])
        num_modules = all_routing_weights[0][0].shape[1]
        
        module_usage = []
        module_specialization = []
        
        for layer_idx in range(num_layers):
            # Collect routing weights for this layer
            layer_weights = [
                batch[layer_idx] for batch in all_routing_weights
            ]
            layer_weights = torch.cat(layer_weights, dim=0)  # [N, num_modules]
            
            # Average usage per module
            avg_usage = layer_weights.mean(dim=0)
            module_usage.append(avg_usage.cpu().numpy())
            
            # Compute specialization (entropy)
            entropy = -(avg_usage * torch.log(avg_usage + 1e-10)).sum()
            max_entropy = np.log(num_modules)
            specialization = 1.0 - (entropy.item() / max_entropy)
            module_specialization.append(specialization)
        
        return {
            'module_usage_per_layer': module_usage,
            'module_specialization_per_layer': module_specialization,
            'avg_specialization': np.mean(module_specialization),
            'num_modules': num_modules,
            'num_layers': num_layers
        }
    
    def _analyze_symbolic(
        self,
        test_loader: DataLoader,
        device: str
    ) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """Analyze symbolic composition model."""
        all_composition_traces = []
        all_selection_traces = []
        
        with torch.no_grad():
            for data, _ in test_loader:
                data = data.to(device)
                _, aux_outputs = self.model(data)
                all_composition_traces.append(aux_outputs['composition_trace'].cpu())
                all_selection_traces.append(aux_outputs['selection_trace'].cpu())
        
        # Concatenate traces
        comp_traces = torch.cat(all_composition_traces, dim=0)  # [N, steps, symbol_dim]
        sel_traces = torch.cat(all_selection_traces, dim=0)  # [N, steps, num_symbols]
        
        # Analyze composition trajectory
        num_steps = comp_traces.shape[1]
        trajectory_changes = []
        
        for step in range(num_steps - 1):
            current = comp_traces[:, step, :]
            next_step = comp_traces[:, step + 1, :]
            change = torch.norm(next_step - current, p=2, dim=1).mean().item()
            trajectory_changes.append(change)
        
        # Analyze symbol usage
        avg_selection = sel_traces.mean(dim=(0, 1))  # [num_symbols]
        symbol_usage_entropy = -(avg_selection * torch.log(avg_selection + 1e-10)).sum().item()
        
        # Find most used symbols
        top_k = 5
        top_symbols = torch.topk(avg_selection, k=top_k)
        
        # Compute symbol consistency (how consistently symbols are selected)
        symbol_consistency = sel_traces.std(dim=0).mean().item()
        
        return {
            'trajectory_changes': trajectory_changes,
            'avg_trajectory_change': np.mean(trajectory_changes),
            'symbol_usage_entropy': symbol_usage_entropy,
            'top_symbols': top_symbols.indices.numpy(),
            'top_symbol_weights': top_symbols.values.numpy(),
            'symbol_consistency': symbol_consistency,
            'num_composition_steps': num_steps
        }
    
    def visualize_analysis(self, analysis_results: Dict[str, any]):
        """
        Print formatted analysis results.
        
        Args:
            analysis_results: Results from analyze_compositionality
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print(f"COMPOSITIONAL ANALYSIS - {self.model_type.upper()}")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        if self.model_type == 'systematic':
            print(f"\nPrimitive Analysis:")
            print(f"  Number of primitives: {analysis_results['num_primitives']}")
            print(f"  Primitive diversity: {analysis_results['primitive_diversity']:.4f} "
                  f"± {analysis_results['primitive_diversity_std']:.4f}")
            print(f"\nRole Analysis:")
            print(f"  Number of roles: {analysis_results['num_roles']}")
            print(f"  Role consistency: {analysis_results['role_consistency']:.4f} "
                  f"± {analysis_results['role_consistency_std']:.4f}")
            print(f"\nBinding Analysis:")
            print(f"  Binding quality: {analysis_results['binding_quality']:.4f} "
                  f"± {analysis_results['binding_quality_std']:.4f}")
        
        elif self.model_type == 'compositional_attn':
            print(f"\nAttention Level Analysis:")
            print(f"  Number of layers: {analysis_results['num_layers']}")
            print(f"  Number of levels: {analysis_results['num_levels']}")
            print(f"  Average level diversity: {analysis_results['avg_level_diversity']:.4f}")
            print(f"\nDiversity per layer:")
            for layer_idx, diversities in enumerate(analysis_results['level_diversity_per_layer']):
                print(f"  Layer {layer_idx}: {np.mean(diversities):.4f}")
        
        elif self.model_type == 'modular':
            print(f"\nModule Analysis:")
            print(f"  Number of modules: {analysis_results['num_modules']}")
            print(f"  Number of layers: {analysis_results['num_layers']}")
            print(f"  Average specialization: {analysis_results['avg_specialization']:.4f}")
            print(f"\nModule usage per layer:")
            for layer_idx, usage in enumerate(analysis_results['module_usage_per_layer']):
                print(f"  Layer {layer_idx}: {usage}")
                print(f"    Specialization: {analysis_results['module_specialization_per_layer'][layer_idx]:.4f}")
        
        elif self.model_type == 'symbolic':
            print(f"\nSymbolic Composition Analysis:")
            print(f"  Number of composition steps: {analysis_results['num_composition_steps']}")
            print(f"  Average trajectory change: {analysis_results['avg_trajectory_change']:.4f}")
            print(f"  Symbol usage entropy: {analysis_results['symbol_usage_entropy']:.4f}")
            print(f"  Symbol consistency: {analysis_results['symbol_consistency']:.4f}")
            print(f"\nTop 5 most used symbols:")
            for idx, (sym_idx, weight) in enumerate(zip(
                analysis_results['top_symbols'],
                analysis_results['top_symbol_weights']
            )):
                print(f"  {idx + 1}. Symbol {sym_idx}: {weight:.4f}")
            print(f"\nTrajectory changes per step:")
            for step, change in enumerate(analysis_results['trajectory_changes']):
                print(f"  Step {step} -> {step + 1}: {change:.4f}")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

def test_zero_shot_generalization():
    """
    Test zero-shot generalization to novel compositions.
    This tests the ability to generalize to unseen combinations of known primitives.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ZERO-SHOT GENERALIZATION TEST")
    print("=" * 80)

    train_primitives = [0, 1, 2, 3]

        (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)  # Only these combinations seen during training
    ]
    
    # Test compositions (novel combinations)
    test_compositions = [
        (0, 2), (1, 3), (0, 3)  # Unseen combinations
    ]
    
    print(f"\nTrain compositions: {train_compositions}")
    print(f"Test compositions (zero-shot): {test_compositions}")
    
    # Create model
    model = SystematicGeneralizationModule(
        input_dim=64,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_primitives=len(train_primitives),
        num_roles=2,
        output_dim=len(train_compositions) + len(test_compositions)
    )
    
    # Generate synthetic data
    def generate_composition_data(compositions, num_samples=100):
        data = []
        labels = []
        for comp_idx, comp in enumerate(compositions):
            for _ in range(num_samples):
                # Create feature vector representing composition
                features = torch.zeros(64)
                for prim_idx
```python
                for prim_idx in comp:
                    start_idx = prim_idx * 16
                    features[start_idx:start_idx + 16] = torch.randn(16)
                
                # Add noise
                features += torch.randn(64) * 0.1
                data.append(features)
                labels.append(comp_idx)
        
        return torch.stack(data), torch.tensor(labels)
    
    # Generate training and test data

    # Adjust test labels to not overlap with train labels
    test_labels += len(train_compositions)
    
    # Create data loaders
    train_dataset = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(train_data, train_labels)
    test_dataset = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(test_data, test_labels)

    # Train model

    print("\nTraining on seen compositions...")

    print(f"\nZero-Shot Results:")

    print(f"  Test Loss: {test_metrics['loss']:.4f}")

    analyzer = CompositionalAnalyzer(model, 'systematic')
    analysis = analyzer.analyze_compositionality(test_loader)
    analyzer.visualize_analysis(analysis)
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)


def test_systematic_vs_iid_generalization():
    """
    Compare systematic generalization vs. i.i.d. generalization.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SYSTEMATIC vs I.I.D. GENERALIZATION COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    input_dim = 64
    output_dim = 12
    
    # Create two types of splits:
    # 1. I.I.D. split: random split of all compositions
    # 2. Systematic split: train on subset of compositions, test on novel combinations
    
    all_compositions = [
        (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3),
        (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3),
        (0, 1, 2), (0, 1, 3), (0, 2, 3), (1, 2, 3),
        (0, 1, 2, 3), (1, 2, 3, 0)
    ]
    
    # I.I.D. split
    np.random.shuffle(all_compositions)
    iid_train = all_compositions[:9]
    iid_test = all_compositions[9:]
    
    # Systematic split (hold out specific primitive combinations)
    systematic_train = [comp for comp in all_compositions if 3 not in comp]
    systematic_test = [comp for comp in all_compositions if 3 in comp]
    
    print(f"\nI.I.D. Split:")
    print(f"  Train: {len(iid_train)} compositions")
    print(f"  Test: {len(iid_test)} compositions")
    
    print(f"\nSystematic Split:")
    print(f"  Train: {len(systematic_train)} compositions (no primitive 3)")
    print(f"  Test: {len(systematic_test)} compositions (contains primitive 3)")
    
    # Generate data for both splits
    def create_split_data(train_comps, test_comps):
        train_data, train_labels = generate_composition_data(train_comps, num_samples=100)
        test_data, test_labels = generate_composition_data(test_comps, num_samples=50)
        
        # Adjust labels
        all_comps = train_comps + test_comps
        label_map = {comp: idx for idx, comp in enumerate(all_comps)}
        
        train_labels = torch.tensor([label_map[train_comps[l.item()]] for l in train_labels])
        test_labels = torch.tensor([label_map[test_comps[l.item() - len(train_comps)]] for l in test_labels])
        
        return train_data, train_labels, test_data, test_labels
    
    def generate_composition_data(compositions, num_samples):
        data = []
        labels = []
        for comp_idx, comp in enumerate(compositions):
            for _ in range(num_samples):
                features = torch.zeros(64)
                for prim_idx in comp:
                    start_idx = prim_idx * 16
                    features[start_idx:start_idx + 16] = torch.randn(16) * 0.5
                features += torch.randn(64) * 0.1
                data.append(features)
                labels.append(comp_idx)
        return torch.stack(data), torch.tensor(labels)
    
    # Test I.I.D. split
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Testing I.I.D. Generalization")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    iid_train_data, iid_train_labels, iid_test_data, iid_test_labels = create_split_data(
        iid_train, iid_test
    )
    
    iid_model = SystematicGeneralizationModule(
        input_dim=input_dim,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_primitives=4,
        num_roles=4,
        output_dim=output_dim
    )
    
    iid_train_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(iid_train_data, iid_train_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=True
    )
    iid_test_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(iid_test_data, iid_test_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=False
    )
    
    iid_trainer = CompositionalTrainer(iid_model, learning_rate=1e-3)
    iid_history = iid_trainer.train(
        iid_train_loader, iid_test_loader,
        num_epochs=25,
        model_type='systematic'
    )
    
    # Test Systematic split
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Testing Systematic Generalization")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    sys_train_data, sys_train_labels, sys_test_data, sys_test_labels = create_split_data(
        systematic_train, systematic_test
    )
    
    sys_model = SystematicGeneralizationModule(
        input_dim=input_dim,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_primitives=4,
        num_roles=4,
        output_dim=output_dim
    )
    
    sys_train_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(sys_train_data, sys_train_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=True
    )
    sys_test_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(sys_test_data, sys_test_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=False
    )
    
    sys_trainer = CompositionalTrainer(sys_model, learning_rate=1e-3)
    sys_history = sys_trainer.train(
        sys_train_loader, sys_test_loader,
        num_epochs=25,
        model_type='systematic'
    )
    
    # Compare results
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print(f"\nI.I.D. Generalization:")
    print(f"  Best Test Accuracy: {max(iid_history['val_accuracy']):.4f}")
    print(f"  Final Test Loss: {iid_history['val_loss'][-1]:.4f}")
    
    print(f"\nSystematic Generalization:")
    print(f"  Best Test Accuracy: {max(sys_history['val_accuracy']):.4f}")
    print(f"  Final Test Loss: {sys_history['val_loss'][-1]:.4f}")
    
    print(f"\nGeneralization Gap:")
    gap = max(iid_history['val_accuracy']) - max(sys_history['val_accuracy'])
    print(f"  Accuracy difference: {gap:.4f}")
    print(f"  {'I.I.D. performs better' if gap > 0 else 'Systematic performs better'}")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)


def test_compositional_transfer():
    """
    Test transfer learning across different compositional tasks.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPOSITIONAL TRANSFER LEARNING TEST")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Task 1: Learn basic compositions
    print("\nTask 1: Learning basic binary compositions...")
    
    task1_model = ModularCompositionalNetwork(
        input_dim=64,
        output_dim=6,
        num_modules=8,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_layers=3,
        routing_mode='soft'
    )
    
    # Generate task 1 data
    task1_comps = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 0), (0, 2), (1, 3)]
    task1_data, task1_labels = generate_composition_data(task1_comps, num_samples=200)
    
    task1_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(task1_data, task1_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=True
    )
    
    # Train on task 1
    task1_trainer = CompositionalTrainer(task1_model, learning_rate=1e-3)
    
    # Simple training loop for task 1
    for epoch in range(20):
        task1_trainer.train_epoch(task1_loader, model_type='modular')
    
    print("Task 1 training complete.")
    
    # Task 2: Learn complex compositions (with transfer)
    print("\nTask 2: Learning complex ternary compositions with transfer...")
    
    # Create new model with same architecture
    task2_model_scratch = ModularCompositionalNetwork(
        input_dim=64,
        output_dim=4,
        num_modules=8,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_layers=3,
        routing_mode='soft'
    )
    
    # Create model with transferred weights
    task2_model_transfer = ModularCompositionalNetwork(
        input_dim=64,
        output_dim=4,
        num_modules=8,
        hidden_dim=128,
        num_layers=3,
        routing_mode='soft'
    )
    
    # Transfer module weights (except output layer)
    with torch.no_grad():
        for (name1, param1), (name2, param2) in zip(
            task1_model.named_parameters(),
            task2_model_transfer.named_parameters()
        ):
            if 'output_projection' not in name1:
                param2.copy_(param1)
    
    # Generate task 2 data
    task2_comps = [(0, 1, 2), (1, 2, 3), (0, 2, 3), (0, 1, 3)]
    
    def generate_composition_data(compositions, num_samples):
        data = []
        labels = []
        for comp_idx, comp in enumerate(compositions):
            for _ in range(num_samples):
                features = torch.zeros(64)
                for prim_idx in comp:
                    start_idx = prim_idx * 16
                    features[start_idx:start_idx + 16] = torch.randn(16) * 0.5
                features += torch.randn(64) * 0.1
                data.append(features)
                labels.append(comp_idx)
        return torch.stack(data), torch.tensor(labels)
    
    task2_train_data, task2_train_labels = generate_composition_data(task2_comps, num_samples=100)
    task2_test_data, task2_test_labels = generate_composition_data(task2_comps, num_samples=50)
    
    task2_train_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(task2_train_data, task2_train_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=True
    )
    task2_test_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(task2_test_data, task2_test_labels),
        batch_size=32, shuffle=False
    )
    
    # Train both models on task 2
    print("Training from scratch...")
    scratch_trainer = CompositionalTrainer(task2_model_scratch, learning_rate=1e-3)
    scratch_history = scratch_trainer.train(
        task2_train_loader, task2_test_loader,
        num_epochs=20,
        model_type='modular'
    )
    
    print("\nTraining with transfer...")
    transfer_trainer = CompositionalTrainer(task2_model_transfer, learning_rate=5e-4)
    transfer_history = transfer_trainer.train(
        task2_train_loader, task2_test_loader,
        num_epochs=20,
        model_type='modular'
    )
    
    # Compare results
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TRANSFER LEARNING RESULTS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print(f"\nFrom Scratch:")
    print(f"  Best Test Accuracy: {max(scratch_history['val_accuracy']):.4f}")
    print(f"  Epochs to best: {np.argmax(scratch_history['val_accuracy']) + 1}")
    
    print(f"\nWith Transfer:")
    print(f"  Best Test Accuracy: {max(transfer_history['val_accuracy']):.4f}")
    print(f"  Epochs to best: {np.argmax(transfer_history['val_accuracy']) + 1}")
    
    improvement = max(transfer_history['val_accuracy']) - max(scratch_history['val_accuracy'])
    print(f"\nTransfer Benefit:")
    print(f"  Accuracy improvement: {improvement:.4f}")
    print(f"  Sample efficiency gain: {(np.argmax(scratch_history['val_accuracy']) - np.argmax(transfer_history['val_accuracy']))} epochs")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

class CompositionalBenchmark:
    """Benchmark suite for compositional generalization patterns."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.results = {}
    
    def benchmark_inference_speed(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        input_
```python
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...],
        num_iterations: int = 100,
        device: str = 'cpu'
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Benchmark inference speed of a model.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to benchmark
            input_shape: Shape of input tensor
            num_iterations: Number of iterations to run
            device: Device to run on
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with timing statistics
        """
        model.to(device)
        model.eval()
        
        # Warm-up
        dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape).to(device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                _ = model(dummy_input)
        
        # Benchmark
        times = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                start_time = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) if device == 'cuda' else None
                end_time = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) if device == 'cuda' else None
                
                if device == 'cuda':
                    start_time.record()
                else:
                    import time
                    start = time.time()
                
                _ = model(dummy_input)
                
                if device == 'cuda':
                    end_time.record()
                    torch.cuda.synchronize()
                    elapsed = start_time.elapsed_time(end_time)
                else:
                    elapsed = (time.time() - start) * 1000  # Convert to ms
                
                times.append(elapsed)
        
        return {
            'mean_time_ms': np.mean(times),
            'std_time_ms': np.std(times),
            'min_time_ms': np.min(times),
            'max_time_ms': np.max(times),
            'throughput_samples_per_sec': 1000.0 / np.mean(times)
        }
    
    def benchmark_memory_usage(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...],
        device: str = 'cpu'
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Benchmark memory usage of a model.
        
        Args:
            model: Model to benchmark
            input_shape: Shape of input tensor
            device: Device to run on
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with memory statistics
        """
        model.to(device)
        
        # Count parameters
        total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        
        # Estimate model size in MB
        param_size_mb = total_params * 4 / (1024 ** 2)  # Assuming float32
        
        # Measure activation memory (approximate)
        model.eval()
        dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape).to(device)
        
        if device == 'cuda':
            torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                _ = model(dummy_input)
            
            peak_memory_mb = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / (1024 ** 2)
        else:
            # For CPU, we can't easily measure memory, so estimate
            peak_memory_mb = param_size_mb * 2  # Rough estimate
        
        return {
            'total_parameters': total_params,
            'trainable_parameters': trainable_params,
            'model_size_mb': param_size_mb,
            'peak_memory_mb': peak_memory_mb
        }
    
    def run_full_benchmark(
        self,
        models: Dict[str, nn.Module],
        input_shape: Tuple[int, ...],
        device: str = 'cpu'
    ) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, any]]:
        """
        Run full benchmark suite on multiple models.
        
        Args:
            models: Dictionary of model_name -> model
            input_shape: Shape of input tensor
            device: Device to run on
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of benchmark results
        """
        results = {}
        
        for model_name, model in models.items():
            print(f"\nBenchmarking {model_name}...")
            
            # Speed benchmark
            speed_results = self.benchmark_inference_speed(
                model, input_shape, num_iterations=100, device=device
            )
            
            # Memory benchmark
            memory_results = self.benchmark_memory_usage(
                model, input_shape, device=device
            )
            
            results[model_name] = {
                'speed': speed_results,
                'memory': memory_results
            }
        
        self.results = results
        return results
    
    def print_benchmark_results(self):
        """Print formatted benchmark results."""
        if not self.results:
            print("No benchmark results available. Run benchmark first.")
            return
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Print table header
        print(f"\n{'Model':<30} {'Params (M)':<12} {'Size (MB)':<12} {'Time (ms)':<12} {'Throughput':<12}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for model_name, results in self.results.items():
            params_m = results['memory']['total_parameters'] / 1e6
            size_mb = results['memory']['model_size_mb']
            time_ms = results['speed']['mean_time_ms']
            throughput = results['speed']['throughput_samples_per_sec']
            
            print(f"{model_name:<30} {params_m:<12.2f} {size_mb:<12.2f} "
                  f"{time_ms:<12.2f} {throughput:<12.1f}")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

def complete_usage_example():
    """
    Complete end-to-end example demonstrating all patterns.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPLETE COMPOSITIONAL GENERALIZATION EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Configuration
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    np.random.seed(42)
    
    input_dim = 64
    hidden_dim = 128
    output_dim = 10
    batch_size = 32
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    print(f"\nUsing device: {device}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 1: Create Models
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 1: Creating Models")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    models = {
        'Systematic Generalization': SystematicGeneralizationModule(
            input_dim=input_dim,
            hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_primitives=8,
            num_roles=4,
            output_dim=output_dim
        ),
        'Modular Compositional': ModularCompositionalNetwork(
            input_dim=input_dim,
            output_dim=output_dim,
            num_modules=6,
            hidden_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_layers=3,
            routing_mode='soft'
        ),
        'Symbolic Composition': SymbolicCompositionNetwork(
            input_dim=input_dim,
            num_symbols=20,
            symbol_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_operators=6,
            num_composition_steps=4,
            output_dim=output_dim
        )
    }
    
    for name, model in models.items():
        num_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        print(f"{name}: {num_params:,} parameters")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 2: Generate Compositional Data
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 2: Generating Compositional Data")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    train_dataset = CompositionalDataset(
        num_samples=1000,
        input_dim=input_dim,
        num_primitives=8,
        num_compositions=output_dim,
        split='train'
    )
    
    val_dataset = CompositionalDataset(
        num_samples=200,
        input_dim=input_dim,
        num_primitives=8,
        num_compositions=output_dim,
        split='val'
    )
    
    test_dataset = CompositionalDataset(
        num_samples=200,
        input_dim=input_dim,
        num_primitives=8,
        num_compositions=output_dim,
        split='test'
    )
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(train_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)
    val_loader = DataLoader(val_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False)
    test_loader = DataLoader(test_dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=False)
    
    print(f"Train samples: {len(train_dataset)}")
    print(f"Validation samples: {len(val_dataset)}")
    print(f"Test samples: {len(test_dataset)}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 3: Train Models
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 3: Training Models")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    trained_models = {}
    training_histories = {}
    
    model_types = {
        'Systematic Generalization': 'systematic',
        'Modular Compositional': 'modular',
        'Symbolic Composition': 'symbolic'
    }
    
    for model_name, model in models.items():
        print(f"\nTraining {model_name}...")
        
        trainer = CompositionalTrainer(model, learning_rate=1e-3, device=device)
        history = trainer.train(
            train_loader, val_loader,
            num_epochs=15,
            model_type=model_types[model_name]
        )
        
        trained_models[model_name] = model
        training_histories[model_name] = history
        
        print(f"Best validation accuracy: {max(history['val_accuracy']):.4f}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 4: Evaluate Models
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 4: Evaluating Models on Test Set")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    test_results = {}
    
    for model_name, model in trained_models.items():
        trainer = CompositionalTrainer(model, device=device)
        metrics = trainer.evaluate(test_loader)
        test_results[model_name] = metrics
        
        print(f"\n{model_name}:")
        print(f"  Test Accuracy: {metrics['accuracy']:.4f}")
        print(f"  Test Loss: {metrics['loss']:.4f}")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 5: Analyze Compositional Properties
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 5: Analyzing Compositional Properties")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for model_name, model in trained_models.items():
        print(f"\nAnalyzing {model_name}...")
        
        analyzer = CompositionalAnalyzer(model, model_types[model_name])
        analysis = analyzer.analyze_compositionality(test_loader, device=device)
        analyzer.visualize_analysis(analysis)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 6: Benchmark Performance
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("Step 6: Benchmarking Performance")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    benchmark = CompositionalBenchmark()
    benchmark_results = benchmark.run_full_benchmark(
        trained_models,
        input_shape=(batch_size, input_dim),
        device=device
    )
    benchmark.print_benchmark_results()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Step 7: Summary and Recommendations
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SUMMARY AND RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Find best model by test accuracy
    best_model_name = max(test_results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['accuracy'])[0]
    best_accuracy = test_results[best_model_name]['accuracy']
    
    # Find fastest model
    fastest_model_name = min(
        benchmark_results.items(),
        key=lambda x: x[1]['speed']['mean_time_ms']
    )[0]
    fastest_time = benchmark_results[fastest_model_name]['speed']['mean_time_ms']
    
    # Find most memory-efficient model
    most_efficient_name = min(
        benchmark_results.items(),
        key=lambda x: x[1]['memory']['model_size_mb']
    )[0]
    smallest_size = benchmark_results[most_efficient_name]['memory']['model_size_mb']
    
    print(f"\nBest Accuracy: {best_model_name} ({best_accuracy:.4f})")
    print(f"Fastest Inference: {fastest_model_name} ({fastest_time:.2f} ms)")
    print(f"Most Memory Efficient: {most_efficient_name} ({smallest_size:.2f} MB)")
    
    print("\nRecommendations:")
    print("  - Use Systematic Generalization for tasks requiring primitive disentanglement")
    print("  - Use Modular Compositional for transfer learning and sample efficiency")
    print("  - Use Symbolic Composition for interpretable reasoning tasks")
    print("  - Use Compositional Attention for sequence-to-sequence tasks")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    
    return {
        'models': trained_models,
        'histories': training_histories,
        'test_results': test_results,
        'benchmark_results': benchmark_results
    }

def save_model_checkpoint(
    model: nn.Module,
    optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
    epoch: int,
    loss: float,
    filepath: str
):
    """
    Save a model checkpoint.
    
    Args:
        model: Model to save
        optimizer: Optimizer state to save
        epoch: Current epoch
        loss: Current loss
        filepath: Path to save checkpoint
    """
    checkpoint = {
        'epoch': epoch,
        'model_state_dict': model.state_dict(),
        'optimizer_state_dict': optimizer.state_dict(),
        'loss': loss,
    }
    torch.save(checkpoint, filepath)
    print(f"Checkpoint saved to {filepath}")


def load_model_checkpoint(
    model: nn.Module,
    optimizer: torch.optim.Optimizer,
    filepath: str,
    device: str = 'cpu'
) -> Tuple[nn.Module, torch.optim.Optimizer, int, float]:
    """
    Load a model checkpoint.
    
    Args:
        model: Model to load weights into
        optimizer: Optimizer to load state into
        filepath: Path to checkpoint
        device: Device to load model on
        
    Returns:
        Tuple of (model, optimizer, epoch, loss)
    """
    checkpoint = torch.load(filepath, map_location=device)
    model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
    optimizer.load_state_dict(checkpoint['optimizer_state_dict'])
    epoch = checkpoint['epoch']
    loss = checkpoint['loss']
    
    print(f"Checkpoint loaded from {filepath}")
    print(f"  Epoch: {epoch}, Loss: {loss:.4f}")
    
    return model, optimizer, epoch, loss


def export_model_to_onnx(
    model: nn.Module,
    input_shape: Tuple[int, ...],
    filepath: str,
    opset_version: int = 11
):
    """
    Export model to ONNX format.
    
    Args:
        model: Model to export
        input_shape: Shape of input tensor
        filepath: Path to save ONNX model
        opset_version: ONNX opset version
    """
    model.eval()
    dummy_input = torch.randn(*input_shape)
    
    torch.onnx.export(
        model,
        dummy_input,
        filepath,
        export_params=True,
        opset_version=opset_version,
        do_constant_folding=True,
        input_names=['input'],
        output_names=['output'],
        dynamic_axes={
            'input': {0: 'batch_size'},
            'output': {0: 'batch_size'}
        }
    )
    print(f"Model exported to ONNX: {filepath}")


def visualize_training_history(
    histories: Dict[str, Dict[str, List[float]]],
    save_path: Optional[str] = None
):
    """
    Visualize training histories (requires matplotlib).
    
    Args:
        histories: Dictionary of model_name -> history dict
        save_path: Optional path to save figure
    """
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(15, 10))
        fig.suptitle('Training Histories Comparison', fontsize=16)
        
        # Plot training loss
        ax = axes[0, 0]
        for model_name, history in histories.items():
            ax.plot(history['train_loss'], label=model_name)
        ax.set_xlabel('Epoch')
        ax.set_ylabel('Loss')
        ax.set_title('Training Loss')
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True)
        
        # Plot validation loss
        ax = axes[0, 1]
        for model_name, history in histories.items():
            ax.plot(history['val_loss'], label=model_name)
        ax.set_xlabel('Epoch')
        ax.set_ylabel('Loss')
        ax.set_title('Validation Loss')
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True)
        
        # Plot validation accuracy
        ax = axes[1, 0]
        for model_name, history in histories.items():
            ax.plot(history['val_accuracy'], label=model_name)
        ax.set_xlabel('Epoch')
        ax.set_ylabel('Accuracy')
        ax.set_title('Validation Accuracy')
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True)
        
        # Plot regularization loss (if available)
        ax = axes[1, 1]
        for model_name, history in histories.items():
            if 'train_reg_loss' in history:
                ax.plot(history['train_reg_loss'], label=model_name)
        ax.set_xlabel('Epoch')
        ax.set_ylabel('Regularization Loss')
        ax.set_title('Regularization Loss')
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(True)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        if save_path:
            plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
            print(f"Figure saved to {save_path}")
        else:
            plt.show()
        
        plt.close()
        
    except ImportError:
        print("Matplotlib not available. Skipping visualization.")

    # 2. Create a model (let's use Systematic Generalization)

    model = SystematicGeneralizationModule(

    )

    val_labels = torch.randint(0, config['output_dim'], (20,))
    
    # 4. Create data loaders
    train_loader = DataLoader(
        torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(train_data, train_labels),
        batch_size=config['batch_size'],
        shuffle=True
    )
    
    val_loader = DataLoader(

    )

class CustomPatternBuilder:
    """
    Builder class for creating custom compositional patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.config = {}
    
    def set_input_dim(self, dim: int) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Set input dimension."""
        self.config['input_dim'] = dim
        return self
    
    def set_output_dim(self, dim: int) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Set output dimension."""
        self.config['output_dim'] = dim
        return self
    
    def set_hidden_dim(self, dim: int) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Set hidden dimension."""
        self.config['hidden_dim'] = dim
        return self
    
    def enable_systematic_generalization(
        self,
        num_primitives: int = 8,
        num_roles: int = 4
    ) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Enable systematic generalization components."""
        self.config['systematic'] = {
            'num_primitives': num_primitives,
            'num_roles': num_roles
        }
        return self
    
    def enable_modular_composition(
        self,
        num_modules: int = 6,
        num_layers: int = 3
    ) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Enable modular composition components."""
        self.config['modular'] = {
            'num_modules': num_modules,
            'num_layers': num_layers
        }
        return self
    
    def enable_symbolic_reasoning(
        self,
        num_symbols: int = 20,
        num_operators: int = 6,
        num_steps: int = 4
    ) -> 'CustomPatternBuilder':
        """Enable symbolic reasoning components."""
        self.config['symbolic'] = {
            'num_symbols': num_symbols,
            'num_operators': num_operators,
            'num_steps': num_steps
        }
        return self
    
    def build(self) -> nn.Module:
        """Build the custom pattern."""
        if 'systematic' in self.config:
            return SystematicGeneralizationModule(
                input_dim=self.config['input_dim'],
                hidden_dim=self.config['hidden_dim'],
                num_primitives=self.config['systematic']['num_primitives'],
                num_roles=self.config['systematic']['num_roles'],
                output_dim=self.config['output_dim']
            )
        elif 'modular' in self.config:
            return ModularCompositionalNetwork(
                input_dim=self.config['input_dim'],
                output_dim=self.config['output_dim'],
                num_modules=self.config['modular']['num_modules'],
                hidden_dim=self.config['hidden_dim'],
                num_layers=self.config['modular']['num_layers']
            )
        elif 'symbolic' in self.config:
            return SymbolicCompositionNetwork(
                input_dim=self.config['input_dim'],
                num_symbols=self.config['symbolic']['num_symbols'],
                symbol_dim=self.config['hidden_dim'],
                num_operators=self.config['symbolic']['num_operators'],
                num_composition_steps=self.config['symbolic']['num_steps'],
                output_dim=self.config['output_dim']
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError("No pattern enabled. Use enable_* methods first.")

"""
Specialized Neural Architecture Components in PyTorch
=====================================================
This module implements five advanced neural architecture patterns:
1. Inverted Residual Block (MobileNetV2)
2. Linear Bottleneck
3. Fused-MBConv (EfficientNetV2)
4. ConvNeXt Block
5. MetaFormer Block
"""

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from typing import Optional, Callable


# ============================================================================
# 1. INVERTED RESIDUAL BLOCK PATTERN (MobileNetV2)
# ============================================================================

class InvertedResidualBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    Inverted Residual Block from MobileNetV2.
    
    Architecture:
    1. Pointwise expansion (1x1 conv)
    2. Depthwise convolution (3x3)
    3. Pointwise projection (1x1 conv)
    
    Key features:
    - Expands channels before depthwise conv
    - Uses linear bottleneck (no activation after final conv)
    - Skip connection when stride=1 and input/output channels match
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        stride: Stride for depthwise convolution
        expand_ratio: Channel expansion ratio (default: 6)
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        stride: int = 1,
        expand_ratio: int = 6
    ):
        super(InvertedResidualBlock, self).__init__()
        
        self.stride = stride
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        # Calculate hidden dimension (expanded channels)
        hidden_dim = int(in_channels * expand_ratio)
        
        layers = []
        
        # Expansion phase (only if expand_ratio != 1)
        if expand_ratio != 1:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Conv2d(in_channels, hidden_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
            ])
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(
                hidden_dim, hidden_dim,
                kernel_size=3, stride=stride, padding=1,
                groups=hidden_dim, bias=False
            ),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        ])
        
        # Projection phase (linear bottleneck - no activation)
        layers.extend([
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        ])
        
        self.conv = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with optional residual connection.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, C, H, W)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (B, out_channels, H', W')
        """
        if self.use_residual:
            return x + self.conv(x)
        else:
            return self.conv(x)


# ============================================================================
# 2. LINEAR BOTTLENECK PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class LinearBottleneck(nn.Module):
    """
    Linear Bottleneck Block.
    
    This pattern reduces dimensionality, applies transformations,
    then expands back, with a linear (no activation) final layer
    to preserve information flow.
    
    Key features:
    - Bottleneck structure: compress -> transform -> expand
    - Linear final layer (no activation)
    - Optional residual connection
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        bottleneck_ratio: Compression ratio (default: 0.25)
        kernel_size: Kernel size for middle convolution
        stride: Stride for middle convolution
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        bottleneck_ratio: float = 0.25,
        kernel_size: int = 3,
        stride: int = 1
    ):
        super(LinearBottleneck, self).__init__()
        
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        
        # Calculate bottleneck dimension
        bottleneck_dim = max(int(in_channels * bottleneck_ratio), 1)
        padding = kernel_size // 2
        
        # Compression phase
        self.compress = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, bottleneck_dim, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_dim),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Transformation phase
        self.transform = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(
                bottleneck_dim, bottleneck_dim,
                kernel_size=kernel_size, stride=stride,
                padding=padding, bias=False
            ),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(bottleneck_dim),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Expansion phase (linear - no activation)
        self.expand = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(bottleneck_dim, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with linear bottleneck.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, C, H, W)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (B, out_channels, H', W')
        """
        identity = x
        
        out = self.compress(x)
        out = self.transform(out)
        out = self.expand(out)
        
        if self.use_residual:
            out = out + identity
        
        return out


# ============================================================================
# 3. FUSED-MBCONV PATTERN (EfficientNetV2)
# ============================================================================

class FusedMBConv(nn.Module):
    """
    Fused Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolution (EfficientNetV2).
    
    Fuses the expansion and depthwise convolution into a single
    regular convolution for better efficiency on modern hardware.
    
    Key features:
    - Fuses expansion + depthwise into single 3x3 conv
    - More efficient than standard MBConv on accelerators
    - Still uses linear bottleneck
    
    Args:
        in_channels: Number of input channels
        out_channels: Number of output channels
        stride: Stride for convolution
        expand_ratio: Channel expansion ratio
        use_se: Whether to use Squeeze-and-Excitation
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_channels: int,
        out_channels: int,
        stride: int = 1,
        expand_ratio: int = 4,
        use_se: bool = False
    ):
        super(FusedMBConv, self).__init__()
        
        self.stride = stride
        self.use_residual = (stride == 1 and in_channels == out_channels)
        self.use_se = use_se
        
        hidden_dim = int(in_channels * expand_ratio)
        
        # Fused expansion and depthwise convolution
        if expand_ratio != 1:
            self.expand_conv = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(
                    in_channels, hidden_dim,
                    kernel_size=3, stride=stride,
                    padding=1, bias=False
                ),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.SiLU(inplace=True)  # SiLU/Swish activation
            )
        else:
            # If no expansion, just use depthwise
            self.expand_conv = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(
                    in_channels, hidden_dim,
                    kernel_size=3, stride=stride,
                    padding=1, bias=False
                ),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(hidden_dim),
                nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
            )
        
        # Squeeze-and-Excitation (optional)
        if use_se:
            self.se = SqueezeExcitation(hidden_dim)
        
        # Projection to output channels (linear)
        self.project = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(hidden_dim, out_channels, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with fused convolution.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, C, H, W)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (B, out_channels, H', W')
        """
        identity = x
        
        out = self.expand_conv(x)
        
        if self.use_se:
            out = self.se(out)
        
        out = self.project(out)
        
        if self.use_residual:
            out = out + identity
        
        return out


class SqueezeExcitation(nn.Module):
    """
    Squeeze-and-Excitation block for channel attention.
    
    Args:
        channels: Number of input channels
        reduction: Reduction ratio for squeeze
    """
    
    def __init__(self, channels: int, reduction: int = 4):
        super(SqueezeExcitation, self).__init__()
        
        reduced_channels = max(1, channels // reduction)
        
        self.se = nn.Sequential(
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
            nn.Conv2d(channels, reduced_channels, kernel_size=1),
            nn.SiLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(reduced_channels, channels, kernel_size=1),
            nn.Sigmoid()
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return x * self.se(x)


# ============================================================================
# 4. CONVNEXT BLOCK PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class ConvNeXtBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    ConvNeXt Block - Modernized ConvNet architecture.
    
    Architecture inspired by Vision Transformers but using convolutions:
    1. Depthwise 7x7 convolution
    2. LayerNorm
    3. Pointwise expansion (4x)
    4. GELU activation
    5. Pointwise projection
    
    Key features:
    - Large kernel depthwise conv (7x7)
    - Inverted bottleneck (expansion in middle)
    - Layer normalization instead of batch norm
    - GELU activation
    - Stochastic depth for regularization
    
    Args:
        dim: Number of input/output channels
        drop_path: Stochastic depth probability
        layer_scale_init: Initial value for layer scale
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        dim: int,
        drop_path: float = 0.0,
        layer_scale_init: float = 1e-6
    ):
        super(ConvNeXtBlock, self).__init__()
        
        # Depthwise convolution with large kernel
        self.dwconv = nn.Conv2d(
            dim, dim,
            kernel_size=7, padding=3,
            groups=dim  # Depthwise
        )
        
        # Layer normalization (applied on channel dimension)
        self.norm = LayerNorm2d(dim)
        
        # Pointwise expansion (4x expansion ratio)
        self.pwconv1 = nn.Linear(dim, 4 * dim)
        self.act = nn.GELU()
        
        # Pointwise projection
        self.pwconv2 = nn.Linear(4 * dim, dim)
        
        # Layer scale (learnable scaling parameter)
        self.gamma = nn.Parameter(
            layer_scale_init * torch.ones(dim),
            requires_grad=True
        ) if layer_scale_init > 0 else None
        
        # Stochastic depth for regularization
        self.drop_path = DropPath(drop_path) if drop_path > 0 else nn.Identity()
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through ConvNeXt block.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, C, H, W)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (B, C, H, W)
        """
        identity = x
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        x = self.dwconv(x)
        
        # Permute to (B, H, W, C) for layer norm and linear layers
        x = x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)
        
        # Normalization
        x = self.norm(x)
        
        # Inverted bottleneck with GELU
        x = self.pwconv1(x)
        x = self.act(x)
        x = self.pwconv2(x)
        
        # Layer scale
        if self.gamma is not None:
            x = self.gamma * x
        
        # Permute back to (B, C, H, W)
        x = x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
        
        # Residual connection with stochastic depth
        x = identity + self.drop_path(x)
        
        return x


class LayerNorm2d(nn.Module):
    """
    Layer Normalization for 2D feature maps.
    Normalizes over the channel dimension.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_channels: int, eps: float = 1e-6):
        super(LayerNorm2d, self).__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(num_channels))
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(num_channels))
        self.eps = eps
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # x shape: (B, H, W, C) or (B, C, H, W)
        if x.dim() == 4 and x.shape[1] != x.shape[-1]:
            # Input is (B, C, H, W), permute to (B, H, W, C)
            x = x.permute(0, 2, 3, 1)
            u = x.mean(-1, keepdim=True)
            s = (x - u).pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
            x = (x - u) / torch.sqrt(s + self.eps)
            x = self.weight * x + self.bias
            return x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
        else:
            # Already in correct format
            u = x.mean(-1, keepdim=True)
            s = (x - u).pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True)
            x = (x - u) / torch.sqrt(s + self.eps)
            return self
```python
            return self.weight * x + self.bias


class DropPath(nn.Module):
    """
    Stochastic Depth (Drop Path) for regularization.
    Randomly drops entire samples during training.
    
    Args:
        drop_prob: Probability of dropping a path
    """
    
    def __init__(self, drop_prob: float = 0.0):
        super(DropPath, self).__init__()
        self.drop_prob = drop_prob
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.drop_prob == 0.0 or not self.training:
            return x
        
        keep_prob = 1 - self.drop_prob
        # Work with different tensor shapes
        shape = (x.shape[0],) + (1,) * (x.ndim - 1)
        random_tensor = keep_prob + torch.rand(shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
        random_tensor.floor_()  # Binarize
        output = x.div(keep_prob) * random_tensor
        return output


# ============================================================================
# 5. METAFORMER BLOCK PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class MetaFormerBlock(nn.Module):
    """
    MetaFormer Block - General architecture abstraction.
    
    MetaFormer is a general architecture that abstracts the token mixer
    (can be attention, pooling, convolution, etc.) from the architecture.
    
    Architecture:
    1. Token Mixer (abstracted - can be any mixing operation)
    2. Layer Norm
    3. MLP (Channel Mixer)
    4. Residual connections
    
    Key features:
    - Separates token mixing from channel mixing
    - Token mixer is pluggable (attention, pooling, conv, etc.)
    - Demonstrates that architecture matters more than specific operations
    
    Args:
        dim: Number of channels
        token_mixer: Token mixing module (e.g., attention, pooling)
        mlp_ratio: MLP expansion ratio
        drop_path: Stochastic depth probability
        layer_scale_init: Initial value for layer scale
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        dim: int,
        token_mixer: Optional[nn.Module] = None,
        mlp_ratio: float = 4.0,
        drop_path: float = 0.0,
        layer_scale_init: float = 1e-6,
        act_layer: Callable = nn.GELU
    ):
        super(MetaFormerBlock, self).__init__()
        
        # Token Mixer (if None, use identity pooling as in PoolFormer)
        if token_mixer is None:
            self.token_mixer = PoolingTokenMixer(pool_size=3)
        else:
            self.token_mixer = token_mixer
        
        # First normalization (before token mixing)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        
        # Layer scale for token mixer
        self.layer_scale1 = nn.Parameter(
            layer_scale_init * torch.ones(dim),
            requires_grad=True
        ) if layer_scale_init > 0 else None
        
        # Drop path
        self.drop_path1 = DropPath(drop_path) if drop_path > 0 else nn.Identity()
        
        # Second normalization (before MLP)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(dim)
        
        # MLP (Channel Mixer)
        mlp_hidden_dim = int(dim * mlp_ratio)
        self.mlp = MLP(
            in_features=dim,
            hidden_features=mlp_hidden_dim,
            act_layer=act_layer
        )
        
        # Layer scale for MLP
        self.layer_scale2 = nn.Parameter(
            layer_scale_init * torch.ones(dim),
            requires_grad=True
        ) if layer_scale_init > 0 else None
        
        # Drop path for MLP
        self.drop_path2 = DropPath(drop_path) if drop_path > 0 else nn.Identity()
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through MetaFormer block.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, C, H, W) or (B, N, C)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of same shape as input
        """
        # Determine if input is 2D (images) or 1D (sequences)
        is_2d = (x.dim() == 4)
        
        if is_2d:
            # Convert (B, C, H, W) to (B, H*W, C)
            B, C, H, W = x.shape
            x = x.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)  # (B, H*W, C)
        
        # Token Mixing with residual
        if self.layer_scale1 is not None:
            x = x + self.drop_path1(
                self.layer_scale1 * self.token_mixer(self.norm1(x))
            )
        else:
            x = x + self.drop_path1(self.token_mixer(self.norm1(x)))
        
        # Channel Mixing (MLP) with residual
        if self.layer_scale2 is not None:
            x = x + self.drop_path2(
                self.layer_scale2 * self.mlp(self.norm2(x))
            )
        else:
            x = x + self.drop_path2(self.mlp(self.norm2(x)))
        
        if is_2d:
            # Convert back to (B, C, H, W)
            x = x.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, H, W)
        
        return x


class PoolingTokenMixer(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple pooling-based token mixer for MetaFormer.
    Uses average pooling as the token mixing operation.
    
    This is used in PoolFormer, which shows that even simple
    pooling can work well in the MetaFormer architecture.
    
    Args:
        pool_size: Size of the pooling window
    """
    
    def __init__(self, pool_size: int = 3):
        super(PoolingTokenMixer, self).__init__()
        self.pool_size = pool_size
        self.pool = nn.AvgPool2d(
            kernel_size=pool_size,
            stride=1,
            padding=pool_size // 2,
            count_include_pad=False
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Apply pooling-based token mixing.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, N, C) or (B, C, H, W)
            
        Returns:
            Mixed tensor with residual subtracted (for residual addition)
        """
        if x.dim() == 3:
            # Convert (B, N, C) to (B, C, H, W) for pooling
            B, N, C = x.shape
            H = W = int(N ** 0.5)
            x_2d = x.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, H, W)
            pooled = self.pool(x_2d)
            pooled = pooled.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
            return pooled - x  # Return difference for residual connection
        else:
            # Already in (B, C, H, W) format
            return self.pool(x) - x


class MLP(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for channel mixing.
    
    Standard MLP with expansion and projection.
    
    Args:
        in_features: Number of input features
        hidden_features: Number of hidden features
        out_features: Number of output features (default: same as input)
        act_layer: Activation function
        drop: Dropout probability
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        in_features: int,
        hidden_features: Optional[int] = None,
        out_features: Optional[int] = None,
        act_layer: Callable = nn.GELU,
        drop: float = 0.0
    ):
        super(MLP, self).__init__()
        
        out_features = out_features or in_features
        hidden_features = hidden_features or in_features
        
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(in_features, hidden_features)
        self.act = act_layer()
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(hidden_features, out_features)
        self.drop = nn.Dropout(drop)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through MLP.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (B, N, C) or (B, C)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of same shape
        """
        x = self.fc1(x)
        x = self.act(x)
        x = self.drop(x)
        x = self.fc2(x)
        x = self.drop(x)
        return x

class MobileNetV2Backbone(nn.Module):
    """
    Example backbone using Inverted Residual Blocks.
    Simplified MobileNetV2 architecture.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000):
        super(MobileNetV2Backbone, self).__init__()
        
        # Initial convolution
        self.conv1 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Inverted residual blocks
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(
            InvertedResidualBlock(32, 16, stride=1, expand_ratio=1),
            InvertedResidualBlock(16, 24, stride=2, expand_ratio=6),
            InvertedResidualBlock(24, 24, stride=1, expand_ratio=6),
            InvertedResidualBlock(24, 32, stride=2, expand_ratio=6),
            InvertedResidualBlock(32, 32, stride=1, expand_ratio=6),
            InvertedResidualBlock(32, 64, stride=2, expand_ratio=6),
            InvertedResidualBlock(64, 64, stride=1, expand_ratio=6),
        )
        
        # Final layers
        self.conv2 = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(64, 1280, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(1280),
            nn.ReLU6(inplace=True)
        )
        
        self.avgpool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(1280, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.conv1(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.conv2(x)
        x = self.avgpool(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


class EfficientNetV2Backbone(nn.Module):
    """
    Example backbone using Fused-MBConv blocks.
    Simplified EfficientNetV2 architecture.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000):
        super(EfficientNetV2Backbone, self).__init__()
        
        # Stem
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, 24, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(24),
            nn.SiLU(inplace=True)
        )
        
        # Fused-MBConv blocks
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(
            FusedMBConv(24, 24, stride=1, expand_ratio=1, use_se=False),
            FusedMBConv(24, 48, stride=2, expand_ratio=4, use_se=False),
            FusedMBConv(48, 48, stride=1, expand_ratio=4, use_se=False),
            FusedMBConv(48, 64, stride=2, expand_ratio=4, use_se=True),
            FusedMBConv(64, 64, stride=1, expand_ratio=4, use_se=True),
            FusedMBConv(64, 128, stride=2, expand_ratio=4, use_se=True),
        )
        
        # Head
        self.head = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(128, 1280, kernel_size=1, bias=False),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(1280),
            nn.SiLU(inplace=True),
            nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1)
        )
        
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(1280, num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.stem(x)
        x = self.blocks(x)
        x = self.head(x)
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = self.classifier(x)
        return x


class ConvNeXtBackbone(nn.Module):
    """
    Example backbone using ConvNeXt blocks.
    Simplified ConvNeXt architecture.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000, depths: list = [3, 3, 9, 3]):
        super(ConvNeXtBackbone, self).__init__()
        
        dims = [96, 192, 384, 768]
        
        # Stem (patchify)
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, dims[0], kernel_size=4, stride=4),
            LayerNorm2d(dims[0])
        )
        
        # Stages
        self.stages = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(4):
            stage = nn.Sequential(
                *[ConvNeXtBlock(
                    dim=dims[i],
                    drop_path=0.1 * (j / sum(depths)),
                    layer_scale_init=1e-6
                ) for j in range(depths[i])]
            )
            self.stages.append(stage)
            
            # Downsample between stages (except last)
            if i < 3:
                downsample = nn.Sequential(
                    LayerNorm2d(dims[i]),
                    nn.Conv2d(dims[i], dims[i+1], kernel_size=2, stride=2)
                )
                self.stages.append(downsample)
        
        # Head
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(dims[-1])
        self.head = nn.Linear(dims[-1], num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.stem(x)
        
        for stage in self.stages:
            x = stage(x)
        
        # Global average pooling
        x = x.mean([-2, -1])  # (B, C)
        x = self.norm(x)
        x = self.head(x)
        return x


class PoolFormerBackbone(nn.Module):
    """
    Example backbone using MetaFormer blocks with pooling.
    PoolFormer architecture.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000, depths: list = [2, 2, 6, 2]):
        super(PoolFormerBackbone, self).__init__()
        
        dims = [64, 128, 320, 512]
        
        # Patch embedding
        self.patch_embed = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, dims[0], kernel_size=7, stride=4, padding=3),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(dims[0])
        )
        
        # Stages
        self.stages = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(4):
            stage = nn.Sequential(
                *[MetaFormerBlock(
                    dim=dims[i],
                    token_mixer=PoolingTokenMixer(pool_size=3),
                    mlp_ratio=4.0,
                    drop_path=0.1 * (j / sum(depths)),
                    layer_scale_init=1e-5
                ) for j in range(depths[i])]
            )
            self.stages.append(stage)
            
            # Downsample between stages (except last)
            if i < 3:
                downsample = nn.Sequential(
                    nn.Conv2d(dims[i], dims[i+1], kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1),
                    nn.BatchNorm2d(dims[i+1])
                )
                self.stages.append(downsample)
        
        # Head
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(dims[-1])
        self.head = nn.Linear(dims[-1], num_classes)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.patch_embed(x)
        
        for stage in self.stages:
            x = stage(x)
        
        # Global average pooling
        x = x.mean([-2, -1])  # (B, C)
        x = self.norm(x)
        x = self.head(x)
        return x

    class CustomMixedNet(nn.Module):
        """
        Example of mixing different block types in one architecture.
        """
        def __init__(self, num_classes: int = 1000):
            super(CustomMixedNet, self).__init__()
            
            self.stem = nn.Sequential(
                nn.Conv2d(3, 32, kernel_size=3, stride=2, padding=1),
                nn.BatchNorm2d(32),
                nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
            )
            
            # Mix different block types
            self.stage1 = nn.Sequential(
                InvertedResidualBlock(32, 64, stride=2, expand_ratio=4),
                InvertedResidualBlock(64, 64, stride=1, expand_ratio=4)
            )
            
            self.stage2 = nn.Sequential(
                FusedMBConv(64, 128, stride=2, expand_ratio=4, use_se=True),
                FusedMBConv(128, 128, stride=1, expand_ratio=4, use_se=True)
            )
            
            self.stage3 = nn.Sequential(
                ConvNeXtBlock(dim=128, drop_path=0.1),
                ConvNeXtBlock(dim=128, drop_path=0.1)
            )
            
            self.head = nn.Sequential(
                nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(1),
                nn.Flatten(),

            )

            x = self.stage1(x)

    import time
    
    def measure_inference_time(model, input_tensor, num_iterations=100):
        """Measure average inference time."""
        model.eval()
        
        # Warmup
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(10):
                _ = model(input_tensor)
        
        # Measure
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(num_iterations):
                _ = model(input_tensor)
        end_time = time.time()
        
        avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / num_iterations * 1000  # ms
        return avg_time
