                    "        axes[idx].imshow(output.numpy(), cmap='RdYlGn', vmin=0, vmax=2)\n",
                    "        axes[idx].set_title(f'Pass {idx+1}')\n",
                    "        axes[idx].axis('off')\n",
                    "    \n",
                    "    plt.suptitle('Dropout (p=0.5) - Different Random Masks', fontsize=14)\n",
                    "    plt.tight_layout()\n",
                    "    plt.show()\n",
                    "\n",
                    "visualize_dropout()"
                ]
            },
            {
                "cell_type": "markdown",
                "metadata": {},
                "source": [
                    "## Complete Training Example\n",
                    "\n",
                    "Train a model with all three patterns."
                ]
            },
            {
                "cell_type": "code",
                "execution_count": None,
                "metadata": {},
                "source": [
                    "# Complete model with all patterns\n",
                    "class CompleteModel(nn.Module):\n",
                    "    def __init__(self):\n",
                    "        super().__init__()\n",
                    "        # Pattern 2: Asymmetric\n",
                    "        self.asym = SimpleAsymmetricBlock(3, 96)\n",
                    "        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(96, 128, 3, padding=1)\n",
                    "        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm2d(128)\n",
                    "        # Pattern 3: Dropout\n",
                    "        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.3)\n",
                    "        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1))\n",
                    "        self.fc = nn.Linear(128, 10)\n",
                    "        # Pattern 1: Init\n",
                    "        self._init_weights()\n",
                    "    \n",
                    "    def _init_weights(self):\n",
                    "        for m in self.modules():\n",
                    "            if isinstance(m, nn.Conv2d):\n",
                    "                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight)\n",
                    "            elif isinstance(m, nn.Linear):\n",
                    "                nn.init.kaiming_normal_(m.weight)\n",
                    "    \n",
                    "    def forward(self, x):\n",
                    "        x = self.asym(x)\n",
                    "        x = F.relu(self.bn(self.conv(x)))\n",
                    "        x = self.dropout(x)\n",
                    "        x = self.pool(x)\n",
                    "        x = x.view(x.size(0), -1)\n",
                    "        return self.fc(x)\n",
                    "\n",
                    "# Quick training loop\n",
                    "model = CompleteModel()\n",
                    "optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)\n",
                    "criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()\n",
                    "\n",
                    "# Synthetic data\n",
                    "X = torch.randn(100, 3, 32, 32)\n",
                    "y = torch.randint(0, 10, (100,))\n",
                    "\n",
                    "losses = []\n",
                    "model.train()\n",
                    "\n",
                    "for epoch in range(20):\n",
                    "    optimizer.zero_grad()\n",
                    "    output = model(X)\n",
                    "    loss = criterion(output, y)\n",
                    "    loss.backward()\n",
                    "    optimizer.step()\n",
                    "    losses.append(loss.item())\n",
                    "\n",
                    "# Plot training curve\n",
                    "plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))\n",
                    "plt.plot(losses, linewidth=2)\n",
                    "plt.xlabel('Epoch')\n",
                    "plt.ylabel('Loss')\n",
                    "plt.title('Training Loss with All Symmetry Breaking Patterns')\n",
                    "plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n",
                    "plt.show()\n",
                    "\n",
                    "print(f'Initial loss: {losses[0]:.4f}')\n",
                    "print(f'Final loss: {losses[-1]:.4f}')\n",
                    "print(f'Improvement: {losses[0] - losses[-1]:.4f}')"
                ]
            },
            {
                "cell_type": "markdown",

# BONUS: COMMAND-LINE INTERFACE
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def create_cli():
    """
    Create a command-line interface for easy access to tools.
    """
    
    cli_code = '''#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Symmetry Breaking Patterns CLI
===============================
Command-line interface for symmetry breaking tools.

Usage:
    python symmetry_breaking_cli.py [command] [options]

Commands:
    init        - Test initialization methods
    train       - Train a model with all patterns
    diagnose    - Run diagnostics on a model
    test        - Run test suite
```python
    visualize   - Generate visualizations
    notebook    - Generate Jupyter notebook
    help        - Show this help message

Examples:
    python symmetry_breaking_cli.py init --method kaiming
    python symmetry_breaking_cli.py train --epochs 10 --lr 0.01
    python symmetry_breaking_cli.py diagnose --model-path model.pth
"""

import argparse
import sys
import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class SymmetryBreakingCLI:
    """Command-line interface for symmetry breaking tools"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            description='Symmetry Breaking Patterns CLI',
            formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
            epilog=__doc__
        )
        self.setup_parser()
    
    def setup_parser(self):
        """Setup argument parser"""
        subparsers = self.parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Available commands')
        
        # Init command
        init_parser = subparsers.add_parser('init', help='Test initialization methods')
        init_parser.add_argument('--method', type=str, default='kaiming',
                                choices=['kaiming', 'xavier', 'orthogonal'],
                                help='Initialization method')
        init_parser.add_argument('--visualize', action='store_true',
                                help='Visualize weight distribution')
        
        # Train command
        train_parser = subparsers.add_parser('train', help='Train a model')
        train_parser.add_argument('--epochs', type=int, default=10,
                                 help='Number of epochs')
        train_parser.add_argument('--lr', type=float, default=0.01,
                                 help='Learning rate')
        train_parser.add_argument('--batch-size', type=int, default=32,
                                 help='Batch size')
        train_parser.add_argument('--dropout', type=float, default=0.3,
                                 help='Dropout probability')
        train_parser.add_argument('--save-path', type=str, default='model.pth',
                                 help='Path to save model')
        
        # Diagnose command
        diag_parser = subparsers.add_parser('diagnose', help='Run diagnostics')
        diag_parser.add_argument('--model-path', type=str, required=True,
                                help='Path to model checkpoint')
        diag_parser.add_argument('--verbose', action='store_true',
                                help='Verbose output')
        
        # Test command
        test_parser = subparsers.add_parser('test', help='Run test suite')
        test_parser.add_argument('--pattern', type=str, default='all',
                                choices=['all', 'init', 'arch', 'stochastic'],
                                help='Which pattern to test')
        
        # Visualize command
        viz_parser = subparsers.add_parser('visualize', help='Generate visualizations')
        viz_parser.add_argument('--type', type=str, default='weights',
                               choices=['weights', 'gradients', 'activations'],
                               help='What to visualize')
        viz_parser.add_argument('--save', type=str, default=None,
                               help='Save visualization to file')
        
        # Notebook command
        nb_parser = subparsers.add_parser('notebook', help='Generate Jupyter notebook')
        nb_parser.add_argument('--output', type=str, default='tutorial.ipynb',
                              help='Output notebook path')
    
    def cmd_init(self, args):
        """Test initialization methods"""
        print(f"\\nTesting {args.method} initialization...")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        layer = nn.Linear(100, 100)
        
        if args.method == 'kaiming':
            nn.init.kaiming_normal_(layer.weight, nonlinearity='relu')
        elif args.method == 'xavier':
            nn.init.xavier_normal_(layer.weight)
        elif args.method == 'orthogonal':
            nn.init.orthogonal_(layer.weight)
        
        weights = layer.weight.data
        print(f"Mean: {weights.mean().item():.6f}")
        print(f"Std:  {weights.std().item():.6f}")
        print(f"Min:  {weights.min().item():.6f}")
        print(f"Max:  {weights.max().item():.6f}")
        
        # Check diversity
        unique_ratio = torch.unique(weights, dim=0).size(0) / weights.size(0)
        print(f"Unique ratio: {unique_ratio:.2%}")
        
        if unique_ratio > 0.95:
            print("✓ Good weight diversity!")
        else:
            print("✗ Warning: Low weight diversity")
        
        if args.visualize:
            import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
            plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
            plt.hist(weights.numpy().flatten(), bins=50, edgecolor='black')
            plt.title(f'{args.method.capitalize()} Initialization')
            plt.xlabel('Weight Value')
            plt.ylabel('Frequency')
            plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
            plt.show()
    
    def cmd_train(self, args):
        """Train a model"""
        print(f"\\nTraining model for {args.epochs} epochs...")
        print("-" * 60)
        print(f"Learning rate: {args.lr}")
        print(f"Batch size: {args.batch_size}")
        print(f"Dropout: {args.dropout}")
        
        # Create model
        from complete_working_example import CompleteWorkingExample
        example = CompleteWorkingExample()
        model, best_acc = example.run()
        
        # Save model
        torch.save({
            'model_state_dict': model.state_dict(),
            'best_acc': best_acc,
            'config': {
                'epochs': args.epochs,
                'lr': args.lr,
                'batch_size': args.batch_size,
                'dropout': args.dropout
            }
        }, args.save_path)
        
        print(f"\\n✓ Model saved to {args.save_path}")
        print(f"  Best accuracy: {best_acc:.2f}%")
    
    def cmd_diagnose(self, args):
        """Run diagnostics on a model"""
        print(f"\\nRunning diagnostics on {args.model_path}...")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Load model
        checkpoint = torch.load(args.model_path)
        
        # Create model and load weights
        # (This is simplified - in practice, you'd need to know the model architecture)
        print("Model checkpoint loaded")
        print(f"Keys in checkpoint: {list(checkpoint.keys())}")
        
        if 'best_acc' in checkpoint:
            print(f"Best accuracy: {checkpoint['best_acc']:.2f}%")
        
        if 'config' in checkpoint:
            print("\\nConfiguration:")
            for key, value in checkpoint['config'].items():
                print(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    def cmd_test(self, args):
        """Run test suite"""
        print(f"\\nRunning tests for: {args.pattern}")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        if args.pattern == 'all':
            run_all_tests()
        else:
            print(f"Running {args.pattern} tests...")
            # Run specific pattern tests
    
    def cmd_visualize(self, args):
        """Generate visualizations"""
        print(f"\\nGenerating {args.type} visualization...")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        
        if args.type == 'weights':
            # Visualize weight distributions
            fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
            methods = ['zero', 'constant', 'xavier', 'kaiming']
            
            for idx, method in enumerate(methods):
                ax = axes[idx // 2, idx % 2]
                layer = nn.Linear(100, 100)
                
                if method == 'zero':
                    nn.init.constant_(layer.weight, 0)
                elif method == 'constant':
                    nn.init.constant_(layer.weight, 0.5)
                elif method == 'xavier':
                    nn.init.xavier_normal_(layer.weight)
                elif method == 'kaiming':
                    nn.init.kaiming_normal_(layer.weight)
                
                weights = layer.weight.data.numpy().flatten()
                ax.hist(weights, bins=50, edgecolor='black')
                ax.set_title(f'{method.capitalize()}\\nStd: {weights.std():.4f}')
                ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
            
            plt.tight_layout()
            
            if args.save:
                plt.savefig(args.save, dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
                print(f"✓ Saved to {args.save}")
            else:
                plt.show()
    
    def cmd_notebook(self, args):
        """Generate Jupyter notebook"""
        print(f"\\nGenerating Jupyter notebook: {args.output}")
        generate_jupyter_notebook()
        print(f"✓ Notebook created: {args.output}")
    
    def run(self):
        """Run the CLI"""
        args = self.parser.parse_args()
        
        if args.command is None:
            self.parser.print_help()
            return
        
        # Dispatch to appropriate command
        cmd_method = getattr(self, f'cmd_{args.command}', None)
        if cmd_method:
            cmd_method(args)
        else:
            print(f"Unknown command: {args.command}")
            self.parser.print_help()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    cli = SymmetryBreakingCLI()
    cli.run()
'''
    
    # Save CLI script
    with open('symmetry_breaking_cli.py', 'w') as f:
        f.write(cli_code)
    
    # Make executable
    import os
    os.chmod('symmetry_breaking_cli.py', 0o755)
    
    print("✓ CLI tool created: symmetry_breaking_cli.py")
    print("  Usage: python symmetry_breaking_cli.py --help")

def generate_config_files():
    """Generate YAML configuration files for different scenarios"""
    
    configs = {
        'base_config.yaml': """
# Base Configuration for Symmetry Breaking Patterns
# ==================================================

model:
  name: "SymmetryBreakingModel"
  input_channels: 3
  num_classes: 10
  base_channels: 64
  depth: 4

# Pattern 1: Initialization
initialization:
  method: "kaiming_normal"  # kaiming_normal, xavier_normal, orthogonal
  nonlinearity: "relu"      # relu, leaky_relu, tanh, sigmoid
  gain: 1.0

# Pattern 2: Architecture
architecture:
  use_asymmetric_blocks: true
  num_branches: 4
  kernel_sizes: [1, 3, 5]
  use_residual: true
  use_batch_norm: true

# Pattern 3: Regularization

  dropout_rate: 0.3
  dropblock_prob: 0.1

# Training

  epochs: 100

"""
Neural Approximation Patterns in PyTorch
========================================
This module implements four fundamental neural approximation patterns:

4. Operator Approximation Pattern

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import torch.optim as optim
from torch.distributions import Normal, MultivariateNormal
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from typing import Callable, Tuple, List, Optional

# ============================================================================
# 1. Universal Approximation Pattern
# ============================================================================

class UniversalApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Universal Approximation Pattern
    
    Implements the Universal Approximation Theorem: a feedforward network
    with a single hidden layer containing a finite number of neurons can
    approximate any continuous function on compact subsets of R^n.
    
    Key Concept: With sufficient width, a shallow network can approximate
    any continuous function to arbitrary precision.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        activation: str = 'relu'
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Dimension of input space
            hidden_dim: Number of neurons in hidden layer (width)
            output_dim: Dimension of output space
            activation: Activation function ('relu', 'tanh', 'sigmoid')
        """
        super(UniversalApproximator, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        
        # Single hidden layer architecture
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        
        # Activation function selection
        self.activation = self._get_activation(activation)
        
    def _get_activation(self, activation: str) -> Callable:
        """Select activation function"""
        activations = {
            'relu': F.relu,
            'tanh': torch.tanh,
            'sigmoid': torch.sigmoid,
            'gelu': F.gelu
        }
        return activations.get(activation, F.relu)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through the universal approximator
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, input_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (batch_size, output_dim)
        """
        x = self.fc1(x)
        x = self.activation(x)
        x = self.fc2(x)
        return x
    
    def fit(
        self,
        target_function: Callable,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        epochs: int = 1000,
        lr: float = 0.001,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> List[float]:
        """
        Train the network to approximate a target function
        
        Args:
            target_function: Function to approximate
            x_train: Training input data
            epochs: Number of training epochs
            lr: Learning rate
            verbose: Whether to print progress
            
        Returns:
            List of loss values during training
        """
        optimizer = optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=lr)
        criterion = nn.MSELoss()
        
        losses = []
        
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            # Generate target outputs
            with torch.no_grad():
                y_target = target_function(x_train)
            
            # Forward pass
            y_pred = self.forward(x_train)
            
            # Compute loss
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_target)
            
            # Backward pass
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            losses.append(loss.item())
            
            if verbose and (epoch + 1) % 100 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/{epochs}], Loss: {loss.item():.6f}")
        
        return losses

class DeepFunctionApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Function Approximation Pattern
    
    Uses deep neural networks to approximate complex functions.
    Unlike universal approximation, this uses depth for better
    representation and generalization.
    
    Key Concept: Deep networks can represent hierarchical features
    and learn compositional functions more efficiently than shallow networks.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dims: List[int],
        output_dim: int,
        activation: str = 'relu',
        use_batch_norm: bool = True,
        dropout_rate: float = 0.0
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Dimension of input space
            hidden_dims: List of hidden layer dimensions
            output_dim: Dimension of output space
            activation: Activation function
            use_batch_norm: Whether to use batch normalization
            dropout_rate: Dropout probability
        """
        super(DeepFunctionApproximator, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.output_dim = output_dim
        self.use_batch_norm = use_batch_norm
        
        # Build network layers
        layers = []
        prev_dim = input_dim
        
        for i, hidden_dim in enumerate(hidden_dims):
            # Linear layer
            layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim))
            
            # Batch normalization
            if use_batch_norm:
                layers.append(nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_dim))
            
            # Activation
            if activation == 'relu':
                layers.append(nn.ReLU())
            elif activation == 'tanh':
                layers.append(nn.Tanh())
            elif activation == 'gelu':
                layers.append(nn.GELU())
            
            # Dropout
            if dropout_rate > 0:
                layers.append(nn.Dropout(dropout_rate))
            
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        # Output layer
        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, output_dim))
        
        self.network = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Forward pass"""
        return self.network(x)
    
    def fit_with_validation(
        self,
        x_train: torch.Tensor,
        y_train: torch.Tensor,
        x_val: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        y_val: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        epochs: int = 1000,
        batch_size: int = 32,
        lr: float = 0.001,
        early_stopping_patience: int = 50
    ) -> Tuple[List[float], List[float]]:
        """
        Train with validation and early stopping
        
        Args:
            x_train: Training inputs
            y_train: Training targets
            x_val: Validation inputs
            y_val: Validation targets
            epochs: Maximum number of epochs
            batch_size: Batch size for training
            lr: Learning rate
            early_stopping_patience: Patience for early stopping
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (train_losses, val_losses)
        """
        optimizer = optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=lr)
        criterion = nn.MSELoss()
        
        train_losses = []
        val_losses = []
        best_val_loss = float('inf')
        patience_counter = 0
        
        # Create data loader
        dataset = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(x_train, y_train)
        dataloader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
            dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True
        )
        
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            # Training phase
            self.train()
            epoch_train_loss = 0.0
            
            for batch_x, batch_y in dataloader:
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                outputs = self.forward(batch_x)
                loss = criterion(outputs, batch_y)
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                epoch_train_loss += loss.item()
            
            avg_train_loss = epoch_train_loss / len(dataloader)
            train_losses.append(avg_train_loss)
            
            # Validation phase
            if x_val is not None and y_val is not None:
                self.eval()
                with torch.no_grad():
                    val_outputs = self.forward(x_val)
                    val_loss = criterion(val_outputs, y_val).item()
                    val_losses.append(val_loss)
                
                # Early stopping check
                if val_loss < best_val_loss:
                    best_val_loss = val_loss
                    patience_counter = 0
                else:
                    patience_counter += 1
                
                if patience_counter >= early_stopping_patience:
                    print(f"Early stopping at epoch {epoch+1}")
                    break
            
            if (epoch + 1) % 100 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/{epochs}], "
                      f"Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.6f}, "
                      f"Val Loss: {val_loss:.6f}" if x_val is not None else "")
        
        return train_losses, val_losses

class DistributionApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Distribution Approximation Pattern
    
    Approximates probability distributions using neural networks.
    Useful for generative modeling, variational inference, and density estimation.
    
    Key Concept: Neural networks can learn to represent complex probability
    distributions by parameterizing distribution parameters.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dims: List[int],
        latent_dim: int,
        distribution_type: str = 'gaussian'
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Dimension of input/observation space
            hidden_dims: Hidden layer dimensions
            latent_dim: Dimension of latent/distribution space
            distribution_type: Type of distribution ('gaussian', 'mixture')
        """
        super(DistributionApproximator, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_dim = input_dim
        self.latent_dim = latent_dim
        self.distribution_type = distribution_type
        
        # Encoder network (maps input to distribution parameters)
        encoder_layers = []
        prev_dim = input_dim
        
        for hidden_dim in hidden_dims:
            encoder_layers.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        self.encoder = nn.Sequential(*encoder_layers)
        
        # Distribution parameter heads
        if distribution_type == 'gaussian':
            # Mean and log variance
            self.mean_head = nn.Linear(prev_dim, latent_dim)
            self.logvar_head = nn.Linear(prev_dim, latent_dim)
        elif distribution_type == 'mixture':
            # Mixture of Gaussians parameters
            self.n_components = 5
            self.pi_head = nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.n_components)  # Mixture weights
            self.mu_head = nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.n_components * latent_dim)
            self.logvar_head = nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.n_components * latent_dim)
        
        # Decoder network (reconstructs input from samples)
        decoder_layers = []
        prev_dim = latent_dim
        
        for hidden_dim in reversed(hidden_dims):
            decoder_layers.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU(),
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        decoder_layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, input_dim))
        self.decoder = nn.Sequential(*decoder_layers)
        
    def encode(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Encode input to distribution parameters
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (mean, logvar) for the distribution
        """
        h = self.encoder(x)
        
        if self.distribution_type == 'gaussian':
            mean = self.mean_head(h)
            logvar = self.logvar_head(h)
            return mean, logvar
        elif self.distribution_type == 'mixture':
            pi = F.softmax(self.pi_head(h), dim=-1)
            mu = self.mu_head(h).view(-1, self.n_components, self.latent_dim)
            logvar = self.logvar_head(h).view(-1, self.n_components, self.latent_dim)
            return (pi, mu, logvar)
    
    def reparameterize(
        self,
        mean: torch.Tensor,
        logvar: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Reparameterization trick for sampling
        
        Args:
            mean: Mean of the distribution
            logvar: Log variance of the distribution
            
        Returns:
            Sampled latent vector
        """
        std = torch.exp(0.5 * logvar)
        eps = torch.randn_like(std)
        return mean + eps * std
    
    def decode(self, z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Decode latent vector to reconstruction"""
        return self.decoder(z)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Full forward pass through VAE
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (reconstruction, mean, logvar)
        """
        mean, logvar = self.encode(x)
        z = self.reparameterize(mean, logvar)
        reconstruction = self.decode(z)
        return reconstruction, mean, logvar
    
    def loss_function(
        self,
        reconstruction: torch.Tensor,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        mean: torch.Tensor,
        logvar: torch.Tensor,
        beta: float = 1.0
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Compute VAE loss (ELBO)
        
        Args:
            reconstruction: Reconstructed input
            x: Original input
            mean: Latent mean
            logvar: Latent log variance
            beta: Weight for KL divergence term
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (total_loss, reconstruction_loss, kl_divergence)
        """
        # Reconstruction loss
        recon_loss = F.mse_loss(reconstruction, x, reduction='sum')
        
        # KL divergence
        kl_div = -0.5 * torch.sum(1 + logvar - mean.pow(2) - logvar.exp())
        
        # Total loss
        total_loss = recon_loss + beta * kl_div
        
        return total_loss, recon_loss, kl_div
    
    def fit(
        self,
        x

    def sample(self, n_samples: int) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Generate samples from the learned distribution
        
        Args:
            n_samples: Number of samples to generate
            
        Returns:
            Generated samples
        """
        self.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            # Sample from standard normal
            z = torch.randn(n_samples, self.latent_dim)
            # Decode to data space
            samples = self.decode(z)
        return samples

class OperatorApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Operator Approximation Pattern
    
    Approximates operators that map between function spaces.
    Used in neural operators, PDE solving, and functional analysis.
    
    Key Concept: Learn mappings between entire functions rather than
    point-wise evaluations. Useful for solving parametric PDEs and
    learning physical operators.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_channels: int,
        output_channels: int,
        hidden_channels: int,
        n_modes: int,
        n_layers: int = 4
    ):
        """
        Fourier Neural Operator architecture
        
        Args:
            input_channels: Number of input function channels
            output_channels: Number of output function channels
            hidden_channels: Hidden dimension size
            n_modes: Number of Fourier modes to use
            n_layers: Number of Fourier layers
        """
        super(OperatorApproximator, self).__init__()
        
        self.input_channels = input_channels
        self.output_channels = output_channels
        self.hidden_channels = hidden_channels
        self.n_modes = n_modes
        self.n_layers = n_layers
        
        # Input projection
        self.fc0 = nn.Linear(input_channels, hidden_channels)
        
        # Fourier layers
        self.fourier_layers = nn.ModuleList([
            FourierLayer(hidden_channels, hidden_channels, n_modes)
            for _ in range(n_layers)
        ])
        
        # Activation
        self.activation = F.gelu
        
        # Output projection
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(hidden_channels, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, output_channels)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through operator network
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch, spatial_dim, input_channels)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (batch, spatial_dim, output_channels)
        """
        # Input projection
        x = self.fc0(x)
        
        # Fourier layers
        for layer in self.fourier_layers:
            x = layer(x)
            x = self.activation(x)
        
        # Output projection
        x = self.fc1(x)
        x = self.activation(x)
        x = self.fc2(x)
        
        return x
    
    def fit_operator(
        self,
        input_functions: torch.Tensor,
        output_functions: torch.Tensor,
        epochs: int = 100,
        batch_size: int = 16,
        lr: float = 0.001,
        verbose: bool = True
    ) -> List[float]:
        """
        Train the operator approximator
        
        Args:
            input_functions: Input function samples (batch, spatial, channels)
            output_functions: Output function samples (batch, spatial, channels)
            epochs: Number of training epochs
            batch_size: Batch size
            lr: Learning rate
            verbose: Whether to print progress
            
        Returns:
            List of losses during training
        """
        optimizer = optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=lr)
        criterion = nn.MSELoss()
        
        dataset = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(input_functions, output_functions)
        dataloader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(
            dataset, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True
        )
        
        losses = []
        
        for epoch in range(epochs):
            epoch_loss = 0.0
            
            for input_batch, output_batch in dataloader:
                # Forward pass
                predictions = self.forward(input_batch)
                
                # Compute loss
                loss = criterion(predictions, output_batch)
                
                # Backward pass
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                
                epoch_loss += loss.item()
            
            avg_loss = epoch_loss / len(dataloader)
            losses.append(avg_loss)
            
            if verbose and (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/{epochs}], Loss: {avg_loss:.6f}")
        
        return losses


class FourierLayer(nn.Module):
    """
    Fourier Layer for Operator Approximation
    
    Implements spectral convolution in Fourier space for learning
    operators between function spaces.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int, n_modes: int):
        """
        Args:
            in_channels: Number of input channels
            out_channels: Number of output channels
            n_modes: Number of Fourier modes to keep
        """
        super(FourierLayer, self).__init__()
        
        self.in_channels = in_channels
        self.out_channels = out_channels
        self.n_modes = n_modes
        
        # Fourier weights (complex-valued)
        self.scale = 1.0 / (in_channels * out_channels)
        self.weights = nn.Parameter(
            self.scale * torch.rand(
                in_channels, out_channels, n_modes, 2, dtype=torch.float32
            )
        )
        
        # Residual connection
        self.residual = nn.Conv1d(in_channels, out_channels, 1)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through Fourier layer
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor (batch, spatial_dim, channels)
            
        Returns:
            Output tensor (batch, spatial_dim, channels)
        """
        batch_size, spatial_dim, channels = x.shape
        
        # Rearrange for convolution: (batch, channels, spatial)
        x_perm = x.permute(0, 2, 1)
        
        # Apply residual connection
        residual = self.residual(x_perm)
        
        # Fourier transform
        x_ft = torch.fft.rfft(x_perm, dim=-1)
        
        # Multiply relevant Fourier modes
        out_ft = torch.zeros(
            batch_size, self.out_channels, spatial_dim // 2 + 1,
            dtype=torch.cfloat, device=x.device
        )
        
        # Complex multiplication in Fourier space
        for i in range(min(self.n_modes, spatial_dim // 2 + 1)):
            # Convert real representation to complex
            weight_complex = torch.view_as_complex(self.weights[:, :, i, :].contiguous())
            # Matrix multiplication
            out_ft[:, :, i] = torch.einsum('bi,io->bo', x_ft[:, :, i], weight_complex)
        
        # Inverse Fourier transform
        x_conv = torch.fft.irfft(out_ft, n=spatial_dim, dim=-1)
        
        # Add residual and rearrange back
        x_out = x_conv + residual
        x_out = x_out.permute(0, 2, 1)
        
        return x_out


class DeepONet(nn.Module):
    """
    Deep Operator Network (DeepONet)
    
    Alternative operator approximation using branch and trunk networks.
    Learns operators by decomposing them into basis functions.
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        branch_input_dim: int,
        trunk_input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        basis_functions: int = 100
    ):
        """
        Args:
            branch_input_dim: Dimension of function input (sensor locations)
            trunk_input_dim: Dimension of evaluation points
            hidden_dim: Hidden layer dimension
            basis_functions: Number of basis functions
        """
        super(DeepONet, self).__init__()
        
        self.basis_functions = basis_functions
        
        # Branch network (processes input function)
        self.branch_net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(branch_input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, basis_functions)
        )
        
        # Trunk network (processes evaluation points)
        self.trunk_net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(trunk_input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, basis_functions)
        )
        
        # Bias term
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1))
        
    def forward(
        self,
        u: torch.Tensor,
        y: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass through DeepONet
        
        Args:
            u: Input function values (batch, sensor_locations)
            y: Evaluation points (batch, n_points, spatial_dim)
            
        Returns:
            Output function values (batch, n_points)
        """
        batch_size, n_points, _ = y.shape
        
        # Branch network output
        branch_out = self.branch_net(u)  # (batch, basis_functions)
        
        # Trunk network output for each evaluation point
        y_flat = y.view(-1, y.shape[-1])  # (batch * n_points, spatial_dim)
        trunk_out = self.trunk_net(y_flat)  # (batch * n_points, basis_functions)
        trunk_out = trunk_out.view(batch_size, n_points, self.basis_functions)
        
        # Inner product between branch and trunk outputs
        output = torch.einsum('bi,bji->bj', branch_out, trunk_out)
        output = output + self.bias
        
        return output

def demo_universal_approximation():
    """Demonstrate Universal Approximation Pattern"""
    print("=" * 70)
    print("1. UNIVERSAL APPROXIMATION PATTERN DEMO")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Define a complex target function
    def target_function(x):
        return torch.sin(3 * x[:, 0:1]) + 0.5 * torch.cos(5 * x[:, 1:2]) + \
               0.3 * x[:, 0:1] * x[:, 1:2]
    
    # Generate training data
    n_samples = 1000
    x_train = torch.rand(n_samples, 2) * 2 - 1  # Range [-1, 1]
    
    # Create and train model
    model = UniversalApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        hidden_dim=100,  # Width for approximation
        output_dim=1,
        activation='tanh'
    )
    
    print(f"\nModel architecture:")
    print(model)
    print(f"\nTotal parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())}")
    
    # Train
    print("\nTraining...")
    losses = model.fit(target_function, x_train, epochs=500, lr=0.01, verbose=True)
    
    # Test

    y_true = target_function(x_test)
    y_pred = model(x_test)
    
    test_error = F.mse_loss(y_pred, y_true).item()
    print(f"\nTest MSE: {test_error:.6f}")
    
    return model, losses

def demo_distribution_approximation():
    """Demonstrate Distribution Approximation Pattern"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("3. DISTRIBUTION APPROXIMATION PATTERN DEMO")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Generate data from a mixture of Gaussians
    def generate_mixture_data(n_samples):
        # Create mixture of 3 Gaussians
        n_per_component = n_samples // 3
        
        # Component 1
        data1 = torch.randn(n_per_component, 2) * 0.5 + torch.tensor([2.0, 2.0])
        
        # Component 2
        data2 = torch.randn(n_per_component, 2) * 0.3 + torch.tensor([-2.0, 2.0])
        
        # Component 3
        data3 = torch.randn(n_samples - 2 * n_per_component, 2) * 0.4 + \
                torch.tensor([0.0, -2.0])
        
        return torch.cat([data1, data2, data3], dim=0)
    
    # Generate training data
    x_train = generate_mixture_data(5000)
    
    print(f"Training data shape: {x_train.shape}")
    print(f"Data mean: {x_train.mean(dim=0)}")
    print(f"Data std: {x_train.std(dim=0)}")
    
    # Create distribution approximator (VAE)
    model = DistributionApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        hidden_dims=[128, 64],
        latent_dim=2,
        distribution_type='gaussian'
    )
    
    print(f"\nModel architecture:")
    print(model)
    print(f"\nTotal parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())}")
    
    # Train
    print("\nTraining VAE...")
    losses = model.fit(
        x_train,
        epochs=100,
        batch_size=128,
        lr=0.001,
        beta=1.0,
        verbose=True
    )
    
    # Generate samples
    print("\nGenerating samples from learned distribution...")
    generated_samples = model.sample(1000)
    
    print(f"Generated samples shape: {generated_samples.shape}")
    print(f"Generated mean: {generated_samples.mean(dim=0)}")
    print(f"Generated std: {generated_samples.std(dim=0)}")
    
    # Reconstruction test
    test_samples = generate_mixture_data(100)
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        reconstructed, mean, logvar = model(test_samples)
    
    recon_error = F.mse_loss(reconstructed, test_samples).item()
    print(f"\nReconstruction MSE: {recon_error:.6f}")
    
    return model, losses, generated_samples


def demo_operator_approximation():
    """Demonstrate Operator Approximation Pattern"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("4. OPERATOR APPROXIMATION PATTERN DEMO")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Generate synthetic operator learning problem
    # Example: Learn the operator that maps initial condition to solution
    # of a simple ODE/PDE
    
    def generate_operator_data(n_samples, n_spatial_points=64):
        """
        Generate data for operator learning
        Example: u(x) -> (u * kernel)(x) (convolution-like operator)
        """
        x = torch.linspace(0, 1, n_spatial_points)
        
        input_functions = []
        output_functions = []
        
        for _ in range(n_samples):
            # Random input function (sum of random Fourier modes)
            n_modes = 5
            coeffs = torch.randn(n_modes, 2)  # amplitude and phase
            
            u_input = torch.zeros(n_spatial_points, 1)
            for k in range(n_modes):
                u_input[:, 0] += coeffs[k, 0] * torch.sin(
                    2 * np.pi * (k + 1) * x + coeffs[k, 1]
                )
            
            # Apply operator (example: derivative + nonlinear term)
            u_output = torch.zeros(n_spatial_points, 1)
            dx = x[1] - x[0]
            
            # Approximate derivative
            u_output[1:-1, 0] = (u_input[2:, 0] - u_input[:-2, 0]) / (2 * dx)
            u_output[0, 0] = (u_input[1, 0] - u_input[0, 0]) / dx
            u_output[-1, 0] = (u_input[-1, 0] - u_input[-2, 0]) / dx
            
            # Add nonlinear term
            u_output[:, 0] += 0.1 * u_input[:, 0]**2
            
            input_functions.append(u_input)
            output_functions.append(u_output)
        
        return torch.stack(input_functions), torch.stack(output_functions)
    
    # Generate training data
    print("Generating operator training data...")
    n_train = 500
    n_spatial = 64
    
    input_funcs, output_funcs = generate_operator_data(n_train, n_spatial)
    
    print(f"Input functions shape: {input_funcs.shape}")
    print(f"Output functions shape: {output_funcs.shape}")
    
    # Create Fourier Neural Operator
    print("\nCreating Fourier Neural Operator...")
    fno_model = OperatorApproximator(
        input_channels=1,
        output_channels=1,
        hidden_channels=64,
        n_modes=16,
        n_layers=4
    )
    
    print(f"\nFNO Model:")
    print(f"Total parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in fno_model.parameters())}")
    
    # Train FNO
    print("\nTraining Fourier Neural Operator...")
    fno_losses = fno_model.fit_operator(
        input_funcs,
        output_funcs,
        epochs=50,
        batch_size=32,
        lr=0.001,
        verbose=True
    )
    
    # Test FNO
    input_test, output_test = generate_operator_data(50, n_spatial)
    fno_model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        predictions = fno_model(input_test)
    
    fno_error = F.mse_loss(predictions, output_test).item()
    print(f"\nFNO Test MSE: {fno_error:.6f}")
    
    # Create DeepONet
    print("\n" + "-" * 70)
    print("Creating DeepONet...")
    
    # For DeepONet, we need sensor locations and evaluation points
    sensor_locations = 32  # Number of sensors
    
    # Sample input functions at sensor locations
    sensor_indices = torch.linspace(0, n_spatial-1, sensor_locations).long()
    branch_inputs = input_funcs[:, sensor_indices, :].squeeze(-1)
    
    # Evaluation points (normalized coordinates)
    eval_points = torch.linspace(0, 1, n_spatial).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(-1)
    eval_points = eval_points.expand(n_train, -1, -1)
    
    deeponet_model = DeepONet(
        branch_input_dim=sensor_locations,
        trunk_input_dim=1,
        hidden_dim=128,
        basis_functions=100
    )
    
    print(f"\nDeepONet Model:")
    print(f"Total parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in deeponet_model.parameters())}")
    
    # Train DeepONet
    print("\nTraining DeepONet...")
    optimizer = optim.Adam(deeponet_model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    
    deeponet_losses = []
    epochs = 50
    
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        
        # Forward pass
        predictions = deeponet_model(branch_inputs, eval_points)
        
        # Reshape predictions and targets
        targets = output_funcs.squeeze(-1)
        
        # Compute loss
        loss = criterion(predictions, targets)
        
        # Backward pass
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        deeponet_losses.append(loss.item())
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
            print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/{epochs}], Loss: {loss.item():.6f}")
    
    # Test DeepONet
    branch_test = input_test[:, sensor_indices, :].squeeze(-1)
    eval_test = eval_points[:50]
    
    deeponet_model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        deeponet_predictions = deeponet_model(branch_test, eval_test)
    
    deeponet_error = F.mse_loss(
        deeponet_predictions,
        output_test.squeeze(-1)
    ).item()
    print(f"\nDeepONet Test MSE: {deeponet_error:.6f}")
    
    return fno_model, deeponet_model, fno_losses, deeponet_losses

# Additional Utility Functions
# ============================================================================

class ApproximationMetrics:
    """Utility class for computing approximation quality metrics"""
    
    @staticmethod
    def l2_error(prediction: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Compute L2 relative error"""
        return torch.norm(prediction - target) / torch.norm(target)
    
    @staticmethod
    def linf_error(prediction: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Compute L-infinity error"""
        return torch.max(torch.abs(prediction - target))
    
    @staticmethod
    def r2_score(prediction: torch.Tensor, target: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Compute R² score"""
        ss_res = torch.sum((target - prediction) ** 2)
        ss_tot = torch.sum((target - torch.mean(target)) ** 2)
        return 1 - (ss_res / ss_tot)
    
    @staticmethod
    def compute_all_metrics(
        prediction: torch.Tensor,
        target: torch.Tensor
    ) -> dict:
        """Compute all approximation metrics"""
        return {
            'mse': F.mse_loss(prediction, target).item(),
            'mae': F.l1_loss(prediction, target).item(),
            'l2_relative_error': ApproximationMetrics.l2_error(prediction, target).item(),
            'linf_error': ApproximationMetrics.linf_error(prediction, target).item(),
            'r2_score': ApproximationMetrics.r2_score(prediction, target).item()
        }


def compare_approximators():
    """Compare different approximation patterns on same task"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("COMPARING APPROXIMATION PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Define a challenging test function
    def test_function(x):
        return torch.sin(5 * x[:, 0:1]) * torch.exp(-x[:, 1:2]**2) + \
               0.5 * torch.tanh(3 * x[:, 0:1] * x[:, 1:2])
    
    # Generate data
    n_train = 2000
    n_test = 500
    
    x_train = torch.rand(n_train, 2) * 4 - 2  # Range [-2, 2]
    y_train = test_function(x_train)
    
    x_test = torch.rand(n_test, 2) * 4 - 2
    y_test = test_function(x_test)
    
    results = {}
    
    # 1. Universal Approximator (Shallow & Wide)
    print("\n[1/3] Testing Universal Approximator...")
    ua_model = UniversalApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        hidden_dim=200,
        output_dim=1,
        activation='tanh'
    )
    ua_model.fit(test_function, x_train, epochs=500, lr=0.01, verbose=False)
    
    ua_model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        ua_pred = ua_model(x_test)
    
    results['Universal Approximator'] = ApproximationMetrics.compute_all_metrics(
        ua_pred, y_test
    )
    
    # 2. Deep Function Approximator
    print("[2/3] Testing Deep Function Approximator...")
    dfa_model = DeepFunctionApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        hidden_dims=[64, 64, 32],
        output_dim=1,
        activation='relu',
        use_batch_norm=True,
        dropout_rate=0.1
    )
    
    dfa_model.fit_with_validation(
        x_train, y_train,
        x_test, y_test,
        epochs=300,
        batch_size=64,
        lr=0.001,
        early_stopping_patience=30
    )
    
    dfa_model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        dfa_pred = dfa_model(x_test)
    
    results['Deep Function Approximator'] = ApproximationMetrics.compute_all_metrics(
        dfa_pred, y_test
    )
    
    # 3. Ensemble of Universal Approximators
    print("[3/3] Testing Ensemble Approximator...")
    
    class EnsembleApproximator(nn.Module):
        def __init__(self, n_models=5):
            super().__init__()
            self.models = nn.ModuleList([
                UniversalApproximator(2, 100, 1, 'tanh')
                for _ in range(n_models)
            ])
        
        def forward(self, x):
            predictions = [model(x) for model in self.models]
            return torch.mean(torch.stack(predictions), dim=0)
    
    ensemble = EnsembleApproximator(n_models=5)
    
    # Train each model in ensemble
    for i, model in enumerate(ensemble.models):
        # Add some randomness to training
        indices = torch.randperm(len(x_train))[:int(0.8 * len(x_train))]
        model.fit(
            test_function,
            x_train[indices],
            epochs=300,
            lr=0.01,
            verbose=False
        )
    
    ensemble.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        ensemble_pred = ensemble(x_test)
    
    results['Ensemble Approximator'] = ApproximationMetrics.compute_all_metrics(
        ensemble_pred, y_test
    )
    
    # Print comparison
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("COMPARISON RESULTS")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    print(f"\n{'Method':<30} {'MSE':<12} {'MAE':<12} {'R² Score':<12}")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    for method, metrics in results.items():
        print(f"{method:<30} {metrics['mse']:<12.6f} "
              f"{metrics['mae']:<12.6f} {metrics['r2_score']:<12.6f}")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    
    return results


def benchmark_approximation_capacity():
    """Benchmark approximation capacity vs network size"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("APPROXIMATION CAPACITY BENCHMARK")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Test function
    def complex_function(x):
        return torch.sin(3*x[:, 0:1]) * torch.cos(2*x[:, 1:2]) + \
               0.5 * torch.exp(-(x[:, 0:1]**2 + x[:, 1:2]**2))
    
    # Generate data
    x_train = torch.rand(1000, 2) * 4 - 2
    x_test = torch.rand(200, 2) * 4 - 2
    y_test = complex_function(x_test)
    
    # Test different network sizes
    hidden_sizes = [10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500]
    results = []
    
    print("\nTesting different network capacities...")
    print(f"{'Hidden Size':<15} {'Parameters':<15} {'Test MSE':<15} {'Training Time (s)':<20}")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    import time
    
    for hidden_size in hidden_sizes:
        model = UniversalApproximator(
            input_dim=2,
            hidden_dim=hidden_size,
            output_dim=1,
            activation='tanh'
        )
        
        n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
        
        # Time training
        start_time = time.time()
        model.fit(complex_function, x_train, epochs=200, lr=0.01, verbose=False)
        training_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Evaluate
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            y_pred = model(x_test)
        
        test_mse = F.mse_loss(y_pred, y_test).item()
        
        results.append({
            'hidden_size': hidden_size,
            'n_params': n_params,
            'test_mse': test_mse,
            'training_time': training_time
        })
        
        print(f"{hidden_size:<15} {n_params:<15} {test_mse:<15.6f} {training_time:<20.2f}")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    
    return results

class MultiTaskApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Multi-task approximator that learns multiple functions simultaneously
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        shared_hidden_dims: List[int],
        task_specific_dims: List[int],
        n_tasks: int
    ):
        """
        Args:
            input_dim: Input dimension
            shared_hidden_dims: Shared layer dimensions
            task_specific_dims: Task-specific layer dimensions
            n_tasks: Number of tasks
        """
        super().__init__()
        
        # Shared layers
        shared_layers = []
        prev_dim = input_dim
        for hidden_dim in shared_hidden_dims:
            shared_layers.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.ReLU()
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        self.shared_network = nn.Sequential(*shared_layers)
        
        # Task-specific heads
        self.task_heads = nn.ModuleList()
        for _ in range(n_tasks):
            task_layers = []
            task_prev_dim = prev_dim
            
            for hidden_dim in task_specific_dims:
                task_layers.extend([
                    nn.Linear(task_prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                    nn.ReLU()
                ])
                task_prev_dim = hidden_dim
            
            task_layers.append(nn.Linear(task_prev_dim, 1))
            self.task_heads.append(nn.Sequential(*task_layers))
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, task_id: int) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass for specific task
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            task_id: Which task to compute
            
        Returns:
            Output for specified task
        """
        shared_features = self.shared_network(x)
        return self.task_heads[task_id](shared_features)
    
    def forward_all_tasks(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> List[torch.Tensor]:
        """Compute outputs for all tasks"""
        shared_features = self.shared_network(x)
        return [head(shared_features) for head in self.task_heads]


def demo_multi_task_approximation():
    """Demonstrate multi-task approximation"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("MULTI-TASK APPROXIMATION DEMO")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Define multiple related tasks
    def task_1(x):
        return torch.sin(x[:, 0:1] * 2) + torch.cos(x[:, 1:2])
    
    def task_2(x):
        return torch.sin(x[:, 0:1] * 2) * 0.5 + torch.exp(-x[:, 1:2]**2)
    
    def task_3(x):
        return torch.cos(x[:, 0:1]) + torch.sin(x[:, 1:2] * 3)
    
    tasks = [task_1, task_2, task_3]
    
    # Generate training data
    n_samples = 1000
    x_train = torch.rand(n_samples, 2) * 4 - 2
    
    # Create multi-task model
    model = MultiTaskApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        shared_hidden_dims=[64, 32],
        task_specific_dims=[16],
        n_tasks=3
    )
    
    print(f"\nModel architecture:")
    print(f"Total parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())}")
    
    # Train on all tasks
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    criterion = nn.MSELoss()
    
    print("\nTraining on multiple tasks...")
    epochs = 200
    
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        total_loss = 0
        
        for task_id, task_func in enumerate(tasks):
            # Generate targets for this task
            y_target = task_func(x_train)
            
            # Forward pass
            y_pred = model(x_train, task_id)
            
            # Compute loss
            loss = criterion(y_pred, y_target)
            total_loss += loss
        
        # Backward pass
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        total_loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 50 == 0:
            print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/{epochs}], Total Loss: {total_loss.item():.6f}")
    
    # Test on all tasks
    x_test = torch.rand(100, 2) * 4 - 2
    
    print("\nTest Results:")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for task_id, task_func in enumerate(tasks):
            y_true = task_func(x_test)
            y_pred = model(x_test, task_id)
            mse = F.mse_loss(y_pred, y_true).item()
            print(f"Task {task_id + 1} MSE: {mse:.6f}")
    
    return model


class ResidualApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Approximator with residual connections for better gradient flow
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        n_residual_blocks: int = 4
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.input_projection = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        
        # Residual blocks
        self.residual_blocks = nn.ModuleList([
            ResidualBlock(hidden_dim) for _ in range(n_residual_blocks)
        ])
        
        self.output_projection = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.input_projection(x)
        
        for block in self.residual_blocks:
            x = block(x)
        
        x = self.output_projection(x)
        return x


class ResidualBlock(nn.Module):
    """Single residual block"""
    def __init__(self, dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.layers = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(dim, dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(dim, dim)
        )
        self.activation = nn.ReLU()
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.activation(x + self.layers(x))


class AttentionApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Approximator using attention mechanisms for adaptive feature weighting
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_dim: int,
        hidden_dim: int,
        output_dim: int,
        n_heads: int = 4
    ):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.input_projection = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        
        # Multi-head attention
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_heads=n_heads,
            batch_first=True
        )
        
        self.feedforward = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim * 4),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 4, hidden_dim)
        )
        
        self.layer_norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        self.layer_norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        
        self.output_projection = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Project input
        x = self.input_projection(x)
        
        # Add batch dimension if needed
        if x.dim() == 2:
            x = x.unsqueeze(1)  # (batch, 1, hidden_dim)
        
        # Self-attention
        attn_out, _ = self.attention(x, x, x)
        x = self.layer_norm1(x + attn_out)
        
        # Feedforward
        ff_out = self.feedforward(x)
        x = self.layer_norm2(x + ff_out)
        
        # Remove sequence dimension and project to output
        x = x.squeeze(1)
        x = self.output_projection(x)
        
        return x

class PhysicsInformedApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) for approximating solutions
    to differential equations
    """
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dims: List[int], output_dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        
        layers = []
        prev_dim = input_dim
        
        for hidden_dim in hidden_dims:
            layers.extend([
                nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim),
                nn.Tanh()  # Tanh often works better for PINNs
            ])
            prev_dim = hidden_dim
        
        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, output_dim))
        self.network = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)
    
    def compute_derivatives(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Compute first and second derivatives using automatic differentiation
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor with requires_grad=True
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (first_derivative, second_derivative)
        """
        u = self.forward(x)
        
        # First derivative
        du_dx = torch.autograd.grad(
            u, x,
            grad_outputs=torch.ones_like(u),
            create_graph=True,
            retain_graph=True
        )[0]
        
        # Second derivative
        d2u_dx2 = torch.autograd.grad(
            du_dx, x,
            grad_outputs=torch.ones_like(du_dx),
            create_graph=True,
            retain_graph=True
        )[0]
        
        return du_dx, d2u_dx2
    
    def physics_loss(
        self,
        x: torch.Tensor,
        boundary_points: torch.Tensor,
        boundary_values: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Compute physics-informed loss
        
        Example: For heat equation ∂u/∂t = α ∂²u/∂x²
        """
        # PDE residual loss
        x.requires_grad_(True)
        u = self.forward(x)
        du_dx, d2u_dx2 = self.compute_derivatives(x)
        
        # Example: Laplace equation ∇²u = 0
        pde_residual = d2u_dx2
        pde_loss = torch.mean(pde_residual**2)
        
        # Boundary condition loss
        u_boundary = self.forward(boundary_points)
        bc_loss = F.mse_loss(u_boundary, boundary_values)
        
        return pde_loss + bc_loss


def demo_physics_informed_approximation():
    """Demonstrate physics-informed neural network"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("PHYSICS-INFORMED APPROXIMATION DEMO")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Problem: Solve Poisson equation -∇²u = f(x) with boundary conditions
    
    # Create model
    model = PhysicsInformedApproximator(
        input_dim=1,
        hidden_dims=[32, 32, 32],
        output_dim=1
    )
    
    print(f"Model parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())}")
    
    # Define domain and boundary
    n_interior = 1000
    n_boundary = 100
    
    # Interior points
    x_interior = torch.rand(n_interior, 1, requires_grad=True) * 2 - 1
    
    # Boundary points
    x_boundary = torch.cat([
        torch.ones(n_boundary // 2, 1) * -1,
        torch.ones(n_boundary // 2, 1) * 1
    ])
    
    # Boundary values (example: u(-1) = 0, u(1) = 0)
    u_boundary = torch.zeros(n_boundary, 1)
    
    # Train
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
    
    print("\nTraining PINN...")
    for epoch in range(1000):
        loss = model.physics_loss(x_interior, x_boundary, u_boundary)
        
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        
        if (epoch + 1) % 200 == 0:
            print(f"Epoch [{epoch+1}/1000], Loss: {loss.item():.6f}")
    
    # Visualize solution
    x_test = torch.linspace(-1, 1, 100).unsqueeze(1)
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        u_pred = model(x_test)
    
    print(f"\nSolution computed at {len(x_test)} points")
    print(f"Solution range: [{u_pred.min().item():.4f}, {u_pred.max().item():.4f}]")
    
    return model


class MetaApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Meta-learning approximator that can quickly adapt to new tasks
    """
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, output_dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        )
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.network(x)
    
    def adapt(
        self,
        x_support: torch.Tensor,
        y_support: torch.Tensor,
        n_steps: int = 5,
        lr: float = 0.01
    ):
        """
        Adapt to new task using support set
        
        Args:
            x_support: Support set inputs
            y_support: Support set outputs
            n_steps: Number of adaptation steps
            lr: Learning rate for adaptation
        """
        # Clone parameters for adaptation
        adapted_params = [p.clone() for p in self.parameters()]
        
        optimizer = optim.SGD([{'params': adapted_params}], lr=lr)
        
        for _ in range(n_steps):
            # Forward pass with adapted parameters
            y_pred = self.forward(x_support)
            loss = F.mse_loss(y_pred, y_support)
            
            # Update adapted parameters
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
        
        return adapted_params


class BayesianApproximator(nn.Module):
    """
    Bayesian neural network for uncertainty-aware approximation
    """
    def __init__(self, input_dim: int, hidden_dim: int, output_dim: int):
        super().__init__()
        
        # Mean parameters
        self.fc1_mean = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.fc2_mean = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
        
        # Log variance parameters
        self.fc1_logvar = nn.Linear(input_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.fc2_logvar = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, output_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, n_samples: int = 1) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Forward pass with uncertainty estimation
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            n_samples: Number of Monte Carlo samples
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (mean_prediction, std_prediction)
        """
        predictions = []
        
        for _ in range(n_samples):
            # Sample weights
            h = self.fc1_mean(x) + torch.randn_like(self.fc1_mean(x)) * \
                torch.exp(0.5 * self.fc1_logvar(x))
            h = F.relu(h)
            
            y = self.fc2_mean(h) + torch.randn_like(self.fc2_mean(h)) * \
                torch.exp(0.5 * self.fc2_logvar(h))
            
            predictions.append(y)
        
        predictions = torch.stack(predictions)
        mean = predictions.mean(dim=0)
        std = predictions.std(dim=0)
        
        return mean, std

class ApproximationTestSuite:
    """Comprehensive test suite for all approximation patterns"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.results = {}
        self.test_functions = self._define_test_functions()
    
    def _define_test_functions(self) -> dict:
        """Define various test functions with different characteristics"""
        return {
            'smooth_polynomial': lambda x: x[:, 0:1]**3 - 2*x[:, 0:1]**2 + x[:, 0:1],
            'trigonometric': lambda x: torch.sin(3*x[:, 0:1]) * torch.cos(2*x[:, 1:2]),
            'discontinuous': lambda x: torch.where(x[:, 0:1] > 0, 
                                                   torch.ones_like(x[:, 0:1]), 
                                                   -torch.ones_like(x[:, 0:1])),
            'high_frequency': lambda x: torch.sin(10*x[:, 0:1]) + 0.1*torch.cos(50*x[:, 1:2]),
            'exponential': lambda x: torch.exp(-x[:, 0:1]**2 - x[:, 1:2]**2),
            'rational': lambda x: 1 / (1 + x[:, 0:1]**2 + x[:, 1:2]**2)
        }
    
    def test_universal_approximation(self, func_name: str) -> dict:
        """Test universal approximation on specific function"""
        print(f"\nTesting Universal Approximation on {func_name}...")
        
        func = self.test_functions[func_name]
        
        # Generate data
        x_train = torch.rand(1000, 2) * 4 - 2
        x_test = torch.rand(200, 2) * 4 - 2
        y_test = func(x_test)
        
        # Test different widths
        widths = [10, 50, 100, 200]
        results = []
        
        for width in widths:
            model = UniversalApproximator(2, width, 1)
            model.fit(func, x_train, epochs=300, lr=0.01, verbose=False)
            
            model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                y_pred = model(x_test)
            
            mse = F.mse_loss(y_pred, y_test).item()
            results.append({'width': width, 'mse': mse})
        
        return results
    
    def test_all_patterns(self) -> dict:
        """Test all patterns on all functions"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print("COMPREHENSIVE APPROXIMATION TEST SUITE")
        print("=" * 70)
        
        all_results = {}
        
        for func_name in self.test_functions.keys():
            print(f"\n{'='*70}")
            print(f"Testing function: {func_name}")
            print(f"{'='*70}")
            
            results = self.test_universal_approximation(func_name)
            all_results[func_name] = results
            
            # Print results
            print(f"\n{'Width':<15} {'MSE':<15}")
            print("-" * 30)
            for r in results:
                print(f"{r['width']:<15} {r['mse']:<15.6f}")
        
        self.results = all_results
        return all_results
    
    def generate_report(self, filename: str = 'approximation_test_report.txt'):
        """Generate detailed test report"""
        with open(filename, 'w') as f:
            f.write("=" * 70 + "\n")
            f.write("NEURAL APPROXIMATION PATTERNS - TEST REPORT\n")
            f.write("=" * 70 + "\n\n")
            
            for func_name, results in self.results.items():
                f.write(f"\nFunction: {func_name}\n")
                f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
                f.write(f"{'Width':<15} {'MSE':<15}\n")
                f.write("-" * 30 + "\n")
                
                for r in results:
                    f.write(f"{r['width']:<15} {r['mse']:<15.6f}\n")
                
                f.write("\n")
        
        print(f"\nTest report saved to '{filename}'")


def run_comprehensive_tests():
    """Run comprehensive test suite"""
    suite = ApproximationTestSuite()
    results = suite.test_all_patterns()
    suite.generate_report()
    return results

def plot_approximation_comparison(
    x_test: torch.Tensor,
    y_true: torch.Tensor,
    predictions: dict,
    title: str = "Approximation Comparison"
):
    """
    Plot comparison of different approximation methods
    
    Args:
        x_test: Test inputs
        y_true: True outputs
        predictions: Dictionary of {method_name: predictions}
        title: Plot title
    """
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(predictions) + 1, figsize=(4*(len(predictions)+1), 4))
        
        # Plot true function
        if x_test.shape[1] == 1:
            axes[0].scatter(x_test.numpy(), y_true.numpy(), alpha=0.5, s=10, label='True')
            axes[0].set_title('True Function')
            axes[0].legend()
            axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
            
            # Plot predictions
            for idx, (name, y_pred) in enumerate(predictions.items()):
                axes[idx+1].scatter(x_test.numpy(), y_true.numpy(), 
                                   alpha=0.3, s=10, label='True', color='blue')
                axes[idx+1].scatter(x_test.numpy(), y_pred.detach().numpy(), 
                                   alpha=0.5, s=10, label='Predicted', color='red')
                axes[idx+1].set_title(name)
                axes[idx+1].legend()
                axes[idx+1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.suptitle(title)
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(f'{title.replace(" ", "_").lower()}.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.show()
        
    except ImportError:
        print("Matplotlib not available for plotting")

        loss.backward()

def example_anomaly_detection():
    """Example: Anomaly detection using distribution approximation"""
    print("\n" + "=" * 70)
    print("EXAMPLE: ANOMALY DETECTION WITH VAE")
    print("=" * 70)
    
    # Generate normal data (2D Gaussian)
    n_normal = 1000
    normal_data = torch.randn(n_normal, 2) * 0.5 + torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0])
    
    # Generate anomalies (far from normal distribution)
    n_anomaly = 50
    anomaly_data = torch.randn(n_anomaly, 2) * 0.3 + torch.tensor([-2.0, -2.0])
    
    print(f"Normal data points: {n_normal}")
    print(f"Anomaly data points: {n_anomaly}")
    
    # Train VAE on normal data only
    model = DistributionApproximator(
        input_dim=2,
        hidden_dims=[64, 32],
        latent_dim=2,
        distribution_type='gaussian'
    )
    
    print("\nTraining VAE on normal data...")
    losses = model.fit(
        normal_data,
        epochs=100,
        batch_size=64,
        lr=0.001,
        beta=1.0,
        verbose=False
    )
    
    print(f"Training completed. Final loss: {losses[-1]:.6f}")
    
    # Compute reconstruction error for normal and anomaly data
    model.eval()
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        # Normal data
        recon_normal, _, _ = model(normal_data[:100])
        error_normal = F.mse_loss(recon_normal, normal_data[:100], reduction='none').mean(dim=1)
        
        # Anomaly data
        recon_anomaly, _, _ = model(anomaly_data)
        error_anomaly = F.mse_loss(recon_anomaly, anomaly_data, reduction='none').mean(dim=1)
    
    # Set threshold (e.g., 95th percentile of normal errors)
    threshold = torch.quantile(error_normal, 0.95)
    
    # Detect anomalies
    detected_anomalies = (error_anomaly > threshold).sum().item()
    
    print(f"\nReconstruction error threshold: {threshold.item():.6f}")
    print(f"Mean error (normal): {error_normal.mean().item():.6f}")
    print(f"Mean error (anomaly): {error_anomaly.mean().item():.6f}")
    print(f"Detected anomalies: {detected_anomalies}/{n_anomaly} ({100*detected_anomalies/n_anomaly:.1f}%)")
    
    return model, threshold, error_normal, error_anomaly
