    cal_size = 750
    test_size = 750
    
    X_train, y_train = X[:train_size], y[:train_size]
    X_cal, y_cal = X[train_size:train_size+cal_size], y[train_size:train_size+cal_size]
    X_test, y_test = X[train_size+cal_size:], y[train_size+cal_size:]
    
    # Create data loaders
    train_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_train, y_train), batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    cal_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_cal, y_cal), batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_test, y_test), batch_size=32)
    
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    print(f"Using device: {device}\n")
    
    # Results storage
    results = {}
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 1. BASELINE (No Calibration)
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*60)
    print("1. BASELINE MODEL (No Calibration)")
    print("="*60)
    
    base_model = create_base_model(num_features=20, num_classes=5)
    base_model = train_base_model(base_model, train_loader, num_epochs=30, device=device)
    
    # Evaluate baseline
    base_model.eval()
    all_probs = []
    all_labels = []
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, labels in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            logits = base_model(inputs)
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            all_probs.append(probs.cpu())
            all_labels.append(labels)
    
    all_probs = torch.cat(all_probs)
    all_labels = torch.cat(all_labels)
    
    predictions = all_probs.argmax(dim=-1)
    accuracy = (predictions == all_labels).float().mean()
    
    # Calculate ECE for baseline
    ece_baseline = calculate_ece(all_probs, all_labels)
    
    results['baseline'] = {
        'accuracy': accuracy.item(),
        'ece': ece_baseline.item()
    }
    
    print(f"Baseline Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
    print(f"Baseline ECE: {ece_baseline:.4f}\n")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 2. ENSEMBLE CALIBRATION
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*60)
    print("2. ENSEMBLE CALIBRATION")
    print("="*60)
    
    # Train ensemble
    print("Training ensemble (3 models)...")
    ensemble_models = []
    for i in range(3):
        print(f"  Training model {i+1}/3...")
        model = create_base_model(num_features=20, num_classes=5)
        model = train_base_model(model, train_loader, num_epochs=25, device=device)
        ensemble_models.append(model)
    
    ensemble = EnsembleCalibratedModel(ensemble_models, num_classes=5)
    ensemble = ensemble.to(device)
    ensemble.calibrate(cal_loader, device=device)
    
    # Evaluate ensemble
    ensemble.eval()
    all_probs_ens = []
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, labels in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            probs = F.softmax(ensemble(inputs), dim=-1)
            all_probs_ens.append(probs.cpu())
    
    all_probs_ens = torch.cat(all_probs_ens)
    predictions_ens = all_probs_ens.argmax(dim=-1)
    accuracy_ens = (predictions_ens == all_labels).float().mean()
    ece_ens = calculate_ece(all_probs_ens, all_labels)
    
    results['ensemble'] = {
        'accuracy': accuracy_ens.item(),
        'ece': ece_ens.item()
    }
    
    print(f"Ensemble Accuracy: {accuracy_ens:.4f}")
    print(f"Ensemble ECE: {ece_ens:.4f}\n")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 3. DISTRIBUTION CALIBRATION
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*60)
    print("3. DISTRIBUTION CALIBRATION")
    print("="*60)
    
    # Use the baseline model for distribution calibration
    dist_cal = DistributionCalibrator(
        base_model=base_model,
        num_classes=5,
        num_bins=15,
        calibration_method='histogram'
    )
    dist_cal = dist_cal.to(device)
    dist_cal.calibrate(cal_loader, device=device)
    
    # Evaluate
    dist_cal.eval()
    all_probs_dist = []
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, labels in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            probs, _ = dist_cal(inputs)
            all_probs_dist.append(probs.cpu())
    
    all_probs_dist = torch.cat(all_probs_dist)
    predictions_dist = all_probs_dist.argmax(dim=-1)
    accuracy_dist = (predictions_dist == all_labels).float().mean()
    ece_dist = calculate_ece(all_probs_dist, all_labels)
    
    results['distribution'] = {
        'accuracy': accuracy_dist.item(),
        'ece': ece_dist.item()
    }
    
    print(f"Distribution Calibration Accuracy: {accuracy_dist:.4f}")
    print(f"Distribution Calibration ECE: {ece_dist:.4f}\n")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 4. CONFORMAL CALIBRATION
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*60)
    print("4. CONFORMAL CALIBRATION")
    print("="*60)
    
    conformal = ConformalCalibrator(
        base_model=base_model,
        num_classes=5,
        coverage_level=0.9,
        method='adaptive'
    )
    conformal = conformal.to(device)
    conformal.calibrate(cal_loader, device=device)
    
    # Evaluate
    coverage_metrics = conformal.evaluate_coverage(test_loader, device=device)
    
    results['conformal'] = {
        'coverage': coverage_metrics['coverage'],
        'target_coverage': coverage_metrics['target_coverage'],
        'avg_set_size': coverage_metrics['average_set_size'],
        'singleton_rate': coverage_metrics['singleton_rate']
    }
    
    print(f"Conformal Coverage: {coverage_metrics['coverage']:.4f} "
          f"(target: {coverage_metrics['target_coverage']:.4f})")
    print(f"Average Set Size: {coverage_metrics['average_set_size']:.2f}")
    print(f"Singleton Rate: {coverage_metrics['singleton_rate']:.4f}\n")
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SUMMARY
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*80)
    print("SUMMARY OF RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    print("\nAccuracy Comparison:")
    print(f"  Baseline:              {results['baseline']['accuracy']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Ensemble:              {results['ensemble']['accuracy']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Distribution Cal.:     {results['distribution']['accuracy']:.4f}")
    
    print("\nCalibration Quality (ECE - lower is better):")
    print(f"  Baseline:              {results['baseline']['ece']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Ensemble:              {results['ensemble']['ece']:.4f}")
    print(f"  Distribution Cal.:     {results['distribution']['ece']:.4f}")
    
    print("\nConformal Prediction:")
    print(f"  Coverage:              {results['conformal']['coverage']:.4f} "
          f"(target: {results['conformal']['target_coverage']:.4f})")
    print(f"  Avg. Set Size:         {results['conformal']['avg_set_size']:.2f}")
    print(f"  Singleton Rate:        {results['conformal']['singleton_rate']:.4f}")
    
    # Visualization
    create_comparison_plot(results)
    
    return results


def calculate_ece(probs: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, n_bins: int = 15) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Calculate Expected Calibration Error."""
    confidences, predictions = probs.max(dim=1)
    accuracies = predictions.eq(labels)
    
    ece = torch.tensor(0.0)
    bin_boundaries = torch.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
    
    for i in range(n_bins):
        bin_lower = bin_boundaries[i]
        bin_upper = bin_boundaries[i + 1]
        
        in_bin = (confidences > bin_lower) & (confidences <= bin_upper)
        prop_in_bin = in_bin.float().mean()
        
        if prop_in_bin > 0:
            accuracy_in_bin = accuracies[in_bin].float().mean()
            avg_confidence_in_bin = confidences[in_bin].mean()
            ece += torch.abs(avg_confidence_in_bin - accuracy_in_bin) * prop_in_bin
    
    return ece


def create_comparison_plot(results: Dict):
    """Create visualization comparing all methods."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))
    
    # Plot 1: Accuracy and ECE comparison
    methods = ['Baseline', 'Ensemble', 'Distribution']
    accuracies = [
        results['baseline']['accuracy'],
        results['ensemble']['accuracy'],
        results['distribution']['accuracy']
    ]
    eces = [
        results['baseline']['ece'],
        results['ensemble']['ece'],
        results['distribution']['ece']
    ]
    
    x = np.arange(len(methods))
    width = 0.35
    
    ax1 = axes[0]
    bars1 = ax1.bar(x - width/2, accuracies, width, label='Accuracy', alpha=0.8)
    ax1.set_ylabel('Accuracy', fontsize=12)
    ax1.set_title('Accuracy Comparison', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    ax1.set_xticks(x)
    ax1.set_xticklabels(methods, rotation=15, ha='right')
    ax1.set_ylim([0, 1])
    ax1.legend(loc='upper left')
    ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    # Add ECE on secondary axis
    ax1_twin = ax1.twinx()
    bars2 = ax1_twin.bar(x + width/2, eces, width, label='ECE', alpha=0.8, color='orange')
    ax1_twin.set_ylabel('ECE (lower is better)', fontsize=12)
    ax1_twin.legend(loc='upper right')
    
    # Add value labels
    for i, (acc, ece) in enumerate(zip(accuracies, eces)):
        ax1.text(i - width/2, acc + 0.02, f'{acc:.3f}', 
                ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
        ax1_twin.text(i + width/2, ece + 0.005, f'{ece:.3f}', 
                     ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)
    
    # Plot 2: Conformal prediction metrics
    ax2 = axes[1]
    
    conf_metrics = ['Coverage', 'Target\nCoverage', 'Singleton\nRate']
    conf_values = [
        results['conformal']['coverage'],
        results['conformal']['target_coverage'],
        results['conformal']['singleton_rate']
    ]
    
    bars = ax2.bar(conf_metrics, conf_values, alpha=0.8, color=['green', 'blue', 'purple'])
    ax2.set_ylabel('Value', fontsize=12)
    ax2.set_title('Conformal Prediction Metrics', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    ax2.set_ylim([0, 1])
    ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')
    
    # Add value labels
    for i, (metric, value) in enumerate(zip(conf_metrics, conf_values)):
        ax2.text(i, value + 0.02, f'{value:.3f}', 
                ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
    
    # Add set size as text
    ax2.text(0.5, 0.5, 
            f"Avg. Set Size:\n{results['conformal']['avg_set_size']:.2f}",
            transform=ax2.transAxes,
            fontsize=11,
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round', facecolor='wheat', alpha=0.5),
            ha='center')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig('calibration_comparison.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print("\nComparison plot saved to 'calibration_comparison.png'")

class CalibrationMetrics:
    """
    Utility class for computing various calibration metrics.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def expected_calibration_error(
        probs: torch.Tensor,
        labels: torch.Tensor,
        n_bins: int = 15
    ) -> float:
        """Compute Expected Calibration Error (ECE)."""
        confidences, predictions = probs.max(dim=1)
        accuracies = predictions.eq(labels)
        
        ece = 0.0
        bin_boundaries = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
        
        for i in range(n_bins):
            bin_lower = bin_boundaries[i]
            bin_upper = bin_boundaries[i + 1]
            
            in_bin = ((confidences > bin_lower) & (confidences <= bin_upper)).cpu().numpy()
            prop_in_bin = np.mean(in_bin)
            
            if prop_in_bin > 0:
                accuracy_in_bin = np.mean(accuracies.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                avg_confidence_in_bin = np.mean(confidences.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                ece += np.abs(avg_confidence_in_bin - accuracy_in_bin) * prop_in_bin
        
        return ece
    
    @staticmethod
    def maximum_calibration_error(
        probs: torch.Tensor,
        labels: torch.Tensor,
        n_bins: int = 15
    ) -> float:
        """Compute Maximum Calibration Error (MCE)."""
        confidences, predictions = probs.max(dim=1)
        accuracies = predictions.eq(labels)
        
        mce = 0.0
        bin_boundaries = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
        
        for i in range(n_bins):
            bin_lower = bin_boundaries[i]
            bin_upper = bin_boundaries[i + 1]
            
            in_bin = ((confidences > bin_lower) & (confidences <= bin_upper)).cpu().numpy()
            prop_in_bin = np.mean(in_bin)
            
            if prop_in_bin > 0:
                accuracy_in_bin = np.mean(accuracies.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                avg_confidence_in_bin = np.mean(confidences.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                mce = max(mce, np.abs(avg_confidence_in_bin - accuracy_in_bin))
        
        return mce
    
    @staticmethod
    def brier_score(probs: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Compute Brier score."""
        num_classes = probs.shape[1]
        one_hot = F.one_hot(labels, num_classes=num_classes).float()
        return torch.mean(torch.sum((probs - one_hot) ** 2, dim=1)).item()
    
    @staticmethod
    def negative_log_likelihood(probs: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """Compute negative log-likelihood."""
        return F.cross_entropy(torch.log(probs + 1e-10), labels).item()
    
    @staticmethod
    def classwise_ece(
        probs: torch.Tensor,
        labels: torch.Tensor,
        n_bins: int = 15
    ) -> Dict[int, float]:
        """Compute ECE for each class separately."""
        num_classes = probs.shape[1]
        classwise_eces = {}
        
        for class_idx in range(num_classes):
            class_probs = probs[:, class_idx]
            class_labels = (labels == class_idx).float()
            
            ece = 0.0
            bin_boundaries = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
            
            for i in range(n_bins):
                bin_lower = bin_boundaries[i]
                bin_upper = bin_boundaries[i + 1]
                
                in_bin = ((class_probs > bin_lower) & (class_probs <= bin_upper)).cpu().numpy()
                prop_in_bin = np.mean(in_bin)
                
                if prop_in_bin > 0:
                    accuracy_in_bin = np.mean(class_labels.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                    avg_confidence_in_bin = np.mean(class_probs.cpu().numpy()[in_bin])
                    ece += np.abs(avg_confidence_in_bin - accuracy_in_bin) * prop_in_bin
            
            classwise_eces[class_idx] = ece
        
        return classwise_eces


class UncertaintyVisualizer:
    """
    Utility class for visualizing uncertainty estimates.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_uncertainty_distribution(
        uncertainties: torch.Tensor,
        correct_mask: torch.Tensor,
        title: str = "Uncertainty Distribution",
        save_path: str = "uncertainty_dist.png"
    ):
        """Plot distribution of uncertainties for correct vs incorrect predictions."""
        uncertainties_np = uncertainties.cpu().numpy()
        correct_np = correct_mask.cpu().numpy()
        
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
        
        # Plot histograms
        ax.hist(uncertainties_np[correct_np], bins=30, alpha=0.6, 
                label='Correct Predictions', color='green', density=True)
        ax.hist(uncertainties_np[~correct_np], bins=30, alpha=0.6, 
                label='Incorrect Predictions', color='red', density=True)
        
        ax.set_xlabel('Uncertainty', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        ax.legend(fontsize=11)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close()
        print(f"Uncertainty distribution plot saved to '{save_path}'")
    
    @staticmethod
    def plot_confidence_histogram(
        confidences: torch.Tensor,
        accuracies: torch.Tensor,
        n_bins: int = 10,
        save_path: str = "confidence_histogram.png"
    ):
        """Plot confidence histogram with accuracy overlay."""
        confidences_np = confidences.cpu().numpy()
        accuracies_np = accuracies.cpu().numpy()
        
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
        
        # Create bins
        bin_boundaries = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
        bin_centers = (bin_boundaries[:-1] + bin_boundaries[1:]) / 2
        
        # Calculate statistics per bin
        bin_counts = []
        bin_accuracies = []
        
        for i in range(n_bins):
            bin_lower = bin_boundaries[i]
            bin_upper = bin_boundaries[i + 1]
            
            in_bin = (confidences_np > bin_lower) & (confidences_np <= bin_upper)
            bin_counts.append(np.sum(in_bin))
            
            if np.sum(in_bin) > 0:
                bin_accuracies.append(np.mean(accuracies_np[in_bin]))
            else:
                bin_accuracies.append(0)
        
        # Plot
        ax.bar(bin_centers, bin_counts, width=0.08, alpha=0.6, 
               label='Sample Count', color='skyblue')
        
        ax2 = ax.twinx()
        ax2.plot(bin_centers, bin_accuracies, 'ro-', linewidth=2, 
                markersize=8, label='Accuracy')
        ax2.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', alpha=0.5, label='Perfect Calibration')
        
        ax.set_xlabel('Confidence', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_ylabel('Sample Count', fontsize=12)
        ax2.set_ylabel('Accuracy', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_title('Confidence Histogram with Accuracy', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        
        ax.legend(loc='upper left')
        ax2.legend(loc='upper right')
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close()
        print(f"Confidence histogram saved to '{save_path}'")

        print(f"  Most Likely: {disease_names[result['point_prediction'][i].item()]}")

        # Clinical interpretation
        if len(pred_set_names) == 1:
            print(f"
```python
            print(f"  ✓ High certainty - Single diagnosis recommended")
        elif len(pred_set_names) == 2:

        else:

# ADVANCED CALIBRATION TECHNIQUES
# ============================================================================

class BayesianTemperatureScaling(nn.Module):
    """
    Advanced temperature scaling with Bayesian inference for uncertainty
    in the temperature parameter itself.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int, num_samples: int = 100):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.num_samples = num_samples
        
        # Prior parameters for temperature (log-normal distribution)
        self.register_buffer('temperature_mean', torch.tensor(0.0))
        self.register_buffer('temperature_std', torch.tensor(0.5))
        
        # Posterior parameters (learned)
        self.posterior_mean = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.0))
        self.posterior_log_std = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(-1.0))
    
    def sample_temperature(self, num_samples: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Sample temperature values from posterior distribution."""
        eps = torch.randn(num_samples, device=self.posterior_mean.device)
        log_temp = self.posterior_mean + eps * torch.exp(self.posterior_log_std)
        return torch.exp(log_temp)
    
    def forward(self, logits: torch.Tensor, num_samples: Optional[int] = None) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with Bayesian temperature scaling.
        
        Returns average of predictions over sampled temperatures.
        """
        if num_samples is None:
            num_samples = self.num_samples
        
        temperatures = self.sample_temperature(num_samples)
        
        # Average predictions over temperature samples
        probs_list = []
        for temp in temperatures:
            scaled_logits = logits / temp
            probs = F.softmax(scaled_logits, dim=-1)
            probs_list.append(probs)
        
        avg_probs = torch.stack(probs_list).mean(dim=0)
        return avg_probs
    
    def fit(self, logits: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, 
            num_iterations: int = 1000, lr: float = 0.01):
        """Fit posterior distribution using variational inference."""
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam([self.posterior_mean, self.posterior_log_std], lr=lr)
        
        for iteration in range(num_iterations):
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            
            # Sample temperature
            temp = self.sample_temperature(1).squeeze()
            
            # Compute likelihood (NLL)
            scaled_logits = logits / temp
            nll = F.cross_entropy(scaled_logits, labels)
            
            # KL divergence from prior
            posterior_std = torch.exp(self.posterior_log_std)
            kl_div = 0.5 * (
                (self.posterior_mean - self.temperature_mean) ** 2 / self.temperature_std ** 2
                + posterior_std ** 2 / self.temperature_std ** 2
                - 1
                + 2 * torch.log(self.temperature_std / posterior_std)
            )
            
            # ELBO loss
            loss = nll + 0.01 * kl_div  # Small weight on KL for regularization
            
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            if (iteration + 1) % 100 == 0:
                print(f"  Iteration {iteration+1}/{num_iterations}, "
                      f"Loss: {loss.item():.4f}, "
                      f"Temp mean: {torch.exp(self.posterior_mean).item():.4f}")


class AdaptiveConformalPrediction(nn.Module):
    """
    Advanced conformal prediction with adaptive quantiles based on
    input features and model uncertainty.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_model: nn.Module, num_classes: int, 
                 coverage_level: float = 0.9):
        super().__init__()
        self.base_model = base_model
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.coverage_level = coverage_level
        
        # Neural network to predict adaptive quantile
        self.quantile_network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(num_classes, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Dropout(0.2),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
            nn.Sigmoid()  # Output between 0 and 1
        )
        
        self.base_quantile = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(0.1))
        self.is_calibrated = False
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """
        Forward pass with adaptive conformal prediction.
        
        Returns:
            (prediction_sets, probabilities, adaptive_quantiles)
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.base_model.eval()
            logits = self.base_model(x)
        
        probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        
        # Predict adaptive quantile for each sample
        adaptive_quantiles = self.quantile_network(probs) * 0.3 + self.base_quantile
        
        # Build prediction sets
        conformity_scores = 1 - probs
        prediction_sets = (conformity_scores <= adaptive_quantiles).float()
        
        return prediction_sets, probs, adaptive_quantiles
    
    def calibrate(self, cal_loader: DataLoader, device: str = 'cuda', 
                  num_epochs: int = 50):
        """Calibrate the adaptive quantile network."""
        self.to(device)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.quantile_network.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            total_coverage = 0
            total_size = 0
            num_batches = 0
            
            for inputs, labels in cal_loader:
                inputs, labels = inputs.to(device), labels.to(device)
                
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                
                prediction_sets, probs, quantiles = self.forward(inputs)
                
                # Calculate coverage
                coverage = prediction_sets[torch.arange(len(labels)), labels].mean()
                
                # Calculate average set size
                set_size = prediction_sets.sum(dim=-1).mean()
                
                # Loss: penalize deviation from target coverage and large set sizes
                coverage_loss = (coverage - self.coverage_level) ** 2
                size_loss = set_size / self.num_classes  # Normalize by num classes
                
                loss = coverage_loss + 0.1 * size_loss
                
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                
                total_coverage += coverage.item()
                total_size += set_size.item()
                num_batches += 1
            
            if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
                avg_coverage = total_coverage / num_batches
                avg_size = total_size / num_batches
                print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}, "
                      f"Coverage: {avg_coverage:.4f}, "
                      f"Avg Set Size: {avg_size:.2f}")
        
        self.is_calibrated = True


class MetaCalibration(nn.Module):
    """
    Meta-learning approach to calibration that learns to calibrate
    across different datasets and domains.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int, hidden_size: int = 64):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        
        # Meta-calibration network that takes logits and outputs calibrated probs
        self.calibration_net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(num_classes, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_size),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, hidden_size),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(hidden_size),
            nn.Dropout(0.3),
            nn.Linear(hidden_size, num_classes),
            nn.Softmax(dim=-1)
        )
    
    def forward(self, logits: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Apply learned calibration transformation."""
        # Use original probabilities as features
        probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        calibrated_probs = self.calibration_net(probs)
        return calibrated_probs
    
    def train_meta_calibration(self, train_loader: DataLoader, 
                               val_loader: DataLoader,
                               num_epochs: int = 100,
                               device: str = 'cuda'):
        """Train meta-calibration network."""
        self.to(device)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=0.001)
        scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(
            optimizer, mode='min', patience=5, factor=0.5
        )
        
        best_val_loss = float('inf')
        
        for epoch in range(num_epochs):
            # Training
            self.train()
            train_loss = 0
            
            for logits, labels in train_loader:
                logits, labels = logits.to(device), labels.to(device)
                
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                
                calibrated_probs = self.forward(logits)
                
                # Multi-objective loss
                nll_loss = F.cross_entropy(torch.log(calibrated_probs + 1e-10), labels)
                brier_loss = F.mse_loss(
                    calibrated_probs,
                    F.one_hot(labels, num_classes=self.num_classes).float()
                )
                
                loss = nll_loss + 0.5 * brier_loss
                
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                
                train_loss += loss.item()
            
            # Validation
            self.eval()
            val_loss = 0
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                for logits, labels in val_loader:
                    logits, labels = logits.to(device), labels.to(device)
                    
                    calibrated_probs = self.forward(logits)
                    nll_loss = F.cross_entropy(
                        torch.log(calibrated_probs + 1e-10), labels
                    )
                    val_loss += nll_loss.item()
            
            avg_train_loss = train_loss / len(train_loader)
            avg_val_loss = val_loss / len(val_loader)
            
            scheduler.step(avg_val_loss)
            
            if avg_val_loss < best_val_loss:
                best_val_loss = avg_val_loss
            
            if (epoch + 1) % 10 == 0:
                print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/{num_epochs}, "
                      f"Train Loss: {avg_train_loss:.4f}, "
                      f"Val Loss: {avg_val_loss:.4f}")

    try:
        conformal = ConformalCalibrator(base_model, num_classes, coverage_level=0.9)
        conformal.to(device)
        conformal.calibrate(val_loader, device)
        
        # Evaluate
        coverage_metrics = conformal.evaluate_coverage(test_loader, device)
        
        coverage_gap = abs(coverage_metrics['coverage'] - coverage_metrics['target_coverage'])
        
        test_results['conformal'] = {
            'status': 'PASSED' if coverage_gap < 0.1 else 'WARNING',
            'coverage': coverage_metrics['coverage'],
            'target': coverage_metrics['target_coverage'],
            'gap': coverage_gap,
            'avg_set_size': coverage_metrics['average_set_size']
        }
        
        if coverage_gap < 0.1:
            print("✓ Conformal Calibration: PASSED")
        else:
            print("⚠ Conformal Calibration: WARNING (coverage gap > 0.1)")
        print(f"  Coverage: {coverage_metrics['coverage']:.4f} "
              f"(target: {coverage_metrics['target_coverage']:.4f})")
        
    except Exception as e:

        print(f"✗ Conformal Calibration: FAILED - {str(e)}")
    
    # Test 4: Multi-Calibration
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("Test 4: Multi-Calibration")
    print("-"*60)
    
    try:
        multi_cal = MultiCalibrator(
            base_model, num_classes,

            num_groups_per_attribute=[2]
        )

        # Create simple validation data with groups
        group_ids_val = torch.randint(0, 2, (len(X_val),))
        
        # Simple calibration test
        print("  Multi-calibration initialized successfully")
        
        test_results['multi'] = {
            'status': 'PASSED',
            'num_groups': 2
        }
        print("✓ Multi-Calibration: PASSED")
        
    except Exception as e:
        test_results['multi'] = {'status': 'FAILED', 'error': str(e)}
        print(f"✗ Multi-Calibration: FAILED - {str(e)}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("TEST SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    passed = sum(1 for r in test_results.values() if r['status'] == 'PASSED')
    total = len(test_results)
    
    print(f"\nTests Passed: {passed}/{total}")
    
    for name, result in test_results.items():
        status_symbol = "✓" if result['status'] == 'PASSED' else "✗"
        print(f"{status_symbol} {name.capitalize()}: {result['status']}")
    
    return test_results

def benchmark_calibration_methods():
    """Benchmark performance of different calibration methods."""
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARKING CALIBRATION METHODS")
    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    import time
    
    # Setup
    num_samples = 1000
    num_features = 20
    num_classes = 5
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    X, y = create_synthetic_dataset(num_samples, num_features, num_classes)
    X_train, y_train = X[:600], y[:600]
    X_cal, y_cal = X[600:800], y[600:800]
    X_test, y_test = X[800:], y[800:]
    
    train_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_train, y_train), batch_size=32)
    cal_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_cal, y_cal), batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_test, y_test), batch_size=32)
    
    # Train base model
    print("Training base model...")
    base_model = create_base_model(num_features, num_classes)
    base_model = train_base_model(base_model, train_loader, num_epochs=30, device=device)
    
    benchmarks = {}
    
    # Benchmark 1: Temperature Scaling (Baseline)
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("Benchmarking: Temperature Scaling")
    print("-"*60)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    temp_scaler = TemperatureScaling(num_classes)
    temp_scaler.to(device)
    
    # Collect calibration data
    all_logits = []
    all_labels = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        base_model.eval()
        for inputs, labels in cal_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            logits = base_model(inputs)
            all_logits.append(logits)
            all_labels.append(labels.to(device))
    
    all_logits = torch.cat(all_logits)
    all_labels = torch.cat(all_labels)
    temp_scaler.fit(all_logits, all_labels)
    
    calibration_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # Inference time
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, _ in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            logits = base_model(inputs)
            _ = temp_scaler(logits)
    inference_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    benchmarks['temperature_scaling'] = {
        'calibration_time': calibration_time,
        'inference_time': inference_time,
        'memory_overhead': 'Minimal (1 parameter)'
    }
    
    print(f"Calibration time: {calibration_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Inference time: {inference_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Benchmark 2: Distribution Calibration
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("Benchmarking: Distribution Calibration")
    print("-"*60)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    dist_cal = DistributionCalibrator(base_model, num_classes, num_bins=15)
    dist_cal.to(device)
    dist_cal.calibrate(cal_loader, device)
    
    calibration_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # Inference time
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, _ in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            _ = dist_cal(inputs)
    inference_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    benchmarks['distribution_calibration'] = {
        'calibration_time': calibration_time,
        'inference_time': inference_time,
        'memory_overhead': f'{num_classes * 15} parameters (bins)'
    }
    
    print(f"Calibration time: {calibration_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Inference time: {inference_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Benchmark 3: Conformal Prediction
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("Benchmarking: Conformal Prediction")
    print("-"*60)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    conformal = ConformalCalibrator(base_model, num_classes, coverage_level=0.9)
    conformal.to(device)
    conformal.calibrate(cal_loader, device)
    
    calibration_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # Inference time
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, _ in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            _ = conformal(inputs)
    inference_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    benchmarks['conformal_prediction'] = {
        'calibration_time': calibration_time,
        'inference_time': inference_time,
        'memory_overhead': 'Minimal (1 threshold)'
    }
    
    print(f"Calibration time: {calibration_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Inference time: {inference_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Benchmark 4: Ensemble Calibration
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("Benchmarking: Ensemble Calibration (3 models)")
    print("-"*60)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    ensemble_models = [base_model] + [
        train_base_model(
            create_base_model(num_features, num_classes),
            train_loader, num_epochs=20, device=device
        ) for _ in range(2)
    ]
    
    ensemble = EnsembleCalibratedModel(ensemble_models, num_classes)
    ensemble.to(device)
    ensemble.calibrate(cal_loader, device)
    
    calibration_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # Inference time
    start_time = time.time()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, _ in test_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            _ = ensemble(inputs)
    inference_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    benchmarks['ensemble_calibration'] = {
        'calibration_time': calibration_time,
        'inference_time': inference_time,
        'memory_overhead': '3x model size + temperature'
    }
    
    print(f"Calibration time: {calibration_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Inference time: {inference_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
    print("="*80 + "\n")
    
    print(f"{'Method':<30} {'Cal. Time (s)':<15} {'Inf. Time (s)':<15} {'Memory':<20}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for method, metrics in benchmarks.items():
        print(f"{method:<30} {metrics['calibration_time']:<15.4f} "
              f"{metrics['inference_time']:<15.4f} {metrics['memory_overhead']:<20}")
    
    return benchmarks

def print_usage_guide():
    """Print comprehensive usage guide for all calibration patterns."""
    
    guide = """
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                    USAGE GUIDE                                         ║
    ║           Advanced Uncertainty Calibration Patterns                    ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    1. ENSEMBLE CALIBRATION PATTERN
    ================================
    
    When to use:
    - Need both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty
    - Can afford multiple model training
    - Want improved accuracy along with calibration
    
    Example:
    ```python
    # Train multiple models
    models = [train_model() for _ in range(5)]
    
    # Create ensemble calibrator
    ensemble = EnsembleCalibratedModel(models, num_classes=10)
    ensemble.calibrate(val_loader)
    
    # Get predictions with uncertainty
    uncertainties = ensemble.get_uncertainty_metrics(x)
    print(f"Epistemic uncertainty: {uncertainties['mutual_information']}")
    ```
    
    2. MULTI-CALIBRATION PATTERN
    ==============================
    
    When to use:
    - Need fairness across different subgroups
    - Have identified sensitive attributes
    - Want to ensure calibration for all demographics
    
    Example:
    ```python
    # Define groups
    multi_cal = MultiCalibrator(
        base_model,
        num_classes=5,
        group_attributes=['gender', 'age'],
        num_groups_per_attribute=[2, 3]
    )
    
    # Calibrate per group
    multi_cal.calibrate_groups(val_loader)
    
    # Predict with group-specific calibration
    preds = multi_cal(x, group_ids={'gender': gender, 'age': age})
    ```
    
    3. DISTRIBUTION CALIBRATION PATTERN
    =====================================
    
    When to use:
    - Need full distribution calibration (not just top-1)
    - Want to improve reliability diagrams
    - Have sufficient calibration data
    
    Example:
    ```python
    # Create distribution calibrator
    dist_cal = DistributionCalibrator(
        base_model,
        num_classes=10,
        num_bins=15,
        calibration_method='histogram'
    )
    
    # Calibrate
    dist_cal.calibrate(cal_loader)
    
    # Get calibrated probabilities
    cal_probs, uncal_probs = dist_cal(x)
    
    # Evaluate
    metrics = dist_cal.evaluate_distribution_calibration(test_loader)
    print(f"ECE improved from {metrics['ece_uncalibrated']:.4f} "
          f"to {metrics['ece_calibrated']:.4f}")
    ```
    
    4. CONFORMAL CALIBRATION PATTERN
    ==================================
    
    When to use:
    - Need guaranteed coverage (e.g., safety-critical applications)
    - Want prediction sets instead of point predictions
    - Have a separate calibration set
    
    Example:
    ```python
    # Create conformal calibrator
    conformal = ConformalCalibrator(
        base_model,
        num_classes=5,
        coverage_level=0.95,  # 95% guaranteed coverage
        method='adaptive'
    )
    
    # Calibrate on holdout set
    conformal.calibrate(cal_loader)
    
    # Get prediction sets
    result = conformal.get_prediction_with_uncertainty(x)
    print(f"Prediction set: {result['prediction_sets']}")
    print(f"Set size (
```python
    print(f"Set size (uncertainty): {result['set_sizes']}")
    
    # Verify coverage
    metrics = conformal.evaluate_coverage(test_loader)
    print(f"Actual coverage: {metrics['coverage']:.2%}")
    ```
    
    CHOOSING THE RIGHT PATTERN
    ===========================
    
    Decision Tree:
    
    1. Do you need guaranteed coverage?
       YES → Use Conformal Calibration
       NO  → Continue to 2
    
    2. Do you have multiple subgroups to protect?
       YES → Use Multi-Calibration
       NO  → Continue to 3
    
    3. Can you train multiple models?
       YES → Use Ensemble Calibration (best overall)
       NO  → Continue to 4
    
    4. Need full distribution calibration?
       YES → Use Distribution Calibration
       NO  → Use simple Temperature Scaling
    
    COMBINING PATTERNS
    ===================
    
    Patterns can be combined for maximum benefit:
    
    ```python
    # Ensemble + Distribution Calibration
    ensemble = EnsembleCalibratedModel(models, num_classes)
    dist_cal = DistributionCalibrator(ensemble, num_classes)
    dist_cal.calibrate(cal_loader)
    
    # Multi-Calibration + Conformal Prediction
    multi_cal = MultiCalibrator(base_model, ...)
    conformal = ConformalCalibrator(multi_cal, ...)
    ```
    
    BEST PRACTICES
    ==============
    
    1. Always use a separate calibration set (not training or test)
    2. Calibration set should be representative of deployment distribution
    3. Monitor calibration metrics over time (distribution shift)
    4. For safety-critical apps, prefer Conformal Prediction
    5. Validate calibration on multiple metrics (ECE, Brier, NLL)
    6. Consider computational constraints (ensemble is expensive)
    7. Document uncertainty estimates for end users
    
    COMMON PITFALLS
    ===============
    
    ✗ Using test set for calibration (data leakage)
    ✗ Too few calibration samples (need 100+ per class)
    ✗ Ignoring distribution shift between cal and test
    ✗ Over-calibrating (too many bins or parameters)
    ✗ Not validating coverage guarantees
    ✗ Mixing up aleatoric vs epistemic uncertainty
    
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║  For more information, run specific demonstrations:                   ║
    ║  python script.py --pattern ensemble                                  ║
    ║  python script.py --pattern multi                                     ║
    ║  python script.py --pattern distribution                              ║
    ║  python script.py --pattern conformal                                 ║
    ║  python script.py --pattern comparison                                ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """
    
    print(guide)

class OnlineCalibration(nn.Module):
    """
    Online calibration that adapts to distribution shift in real-time.
    Useful for deployment scenarios where data distribution changes.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_model: nn.Module, num_classes: int, 
                 window_size: int = 100, learning_rate: float = 0.01):
        super().__init__()
        self.base_model = base_model
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.learning_rate = learning_rate
        
        # Temperature parameter
        self.temperature = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1) * 1.5)
        
        # Sliding window of recent predictions and labels
        self.register_buffer('recent_logits', torch.zeros(window_size, num_classes))
        self.register_buffer('recent_labels', torch.zeros(window_size, dtype=torch.long))
        self.register_buffer('buffer_index', torch.tensor(0))
        self.register_buffer('buffer_full', torch.tensor(False))
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Forward pass with current temperature."""
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.base_model.eval()
            logits = self.base_model(x)
        
        return logits / self.temperature
    
    def update(self, logits: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor):
        """
        Update calibration based on new observations.
        
        Args:
            logits: Model logits for new samples
            labels: True labels for new samples
        """
        batch_size = logits.size(0)
        
        # Add to buffer
        for i in range(batch_size):
            idx = self.buffer_index.item()
            self.recent_logits[idx] = logits[i].detach()
            self.recent_labels[idx] = labels[i].detach()
            
            self.buffer_index = (self.buffer_index + 1) % self.window_size
            
            if self.buffer_index == 0:
                self.buffer_full = torch.tensor(True)
        
        # Recalibrate if buffer has enough samples
        if self.buffer_full or self.buffer_index > 20:
            self._recalibrate()
    
    def _recalibrate(self):
        """Recalibrate temperature using recent observations."""
        if self.buffer_full:
            logits = self.recent_logits
            labels = self.recent_labels
        else:
            logits = self.recent_logits[:self.buffer_index]
            labels = self.recent_labels[:self.buffer_index]
        
        # Simple gradient descent step
        optimizer = torch.optim.SGD([self.temperature], lr=self.learning_rate)
        
        for _ in range(5):  # Few iterations
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss = F.cross_entropy(logits / self.temperature, labels)
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            
            # Clamp temperature to reasonable range
            with torch.no_grad():
                self.temperature.clamp_(0.1, 10.0)


class HierarchicalCalibration(nn.Module):
    """
    Hierarchical calibration for problems with class hierarchies.
    Calibrates at multiple levels of the hierarchy.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_model: nn.Module, class_hierarchy: Dict[int, List[int]]):
        """
        Args:
            base_model: Base prediction model
            class_hierarchy: Dict mapping parent classes to child classes
                           e.g., {0: [1, 2], 1: [3, 4, 5]} means class 0 has children 1,2
        """
        super().__init__()
        self.base_model = base_model
        self.class_hierarchy = class_hierarchy
        
        # Temperature for each level
        self.level_temperatures = nn.ParameterDict()
        for level in range(self._get_max_depth()):
            self.level_temperatures[f'level_{level}'] = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1) * 1.5)
    
    def _get_max_depth(self) -> int:
        """Calculate maximum depth of hierarchy."""
        def get_depth(node, current_depth=0):
            if node not in self.class_hierarchy:
                return current_depth
            return max(get_depth(child, current_depth + 1) 
                      for child in self.class_hierarchy[node])
        
        return max(get_depth(root) for root in self.class_hierarchy.keys())
    
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, level: int = 0) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Forward pass with hierarchical calibration.
        
        Args:
            x: Input tensor
            level: Hierarchy level to calibrate at
        """
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.base_model.eval()
            logits = self.base_model(x)
        
        temp_key = f'level_{level}'
        if temp_key in self.level_temperatures:
            temperature = self.level_temperatures[temp_key]
        else:
            temperature = torch.tensor(1.0)
        
        return logits / temperature


class CalibrationMonitor:
    """
    Monitor calibration metrics over time to detect distribution shift
    and calibration degradation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_classes: int, window_size: int = 1000):
        self.num_classes = num_classes
        self.window_size = window_size
        
        # History of metrics
        self.ece_history = []
        self.accuracy_history = []
        self.confidence_history = []
        self.timestamps = []
        
        # Sliding window
        self.recent_predictions = []
        self.recent_labels = []
        self.recent_confidences = []
    
    def update(self, predictions: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, 
               probabilities: torch.Tensor):
        """Update monitor with new predictions."""
        import datetime
        
        batch_size = predictions.size(0)
        confidences = probabilities.max(dim=-1)[0]
        
        # Add to sliding window
        self.recent_predictions.extend(predictions.cpu().tolist())
        self.recent_labels.extend(labels.cpu().tolist())
        self.recent_confidences.extend(confidences.cpu().tolist())
        
        # Trim to window size
        if len(self.recent_predictions) > self.window_size:
            self.recent_predictions = self.recent_predictions[-self.window_size:]
            self.recent_labels = self.recent_labels[-self.window_size:]
            self.recent_confidences = self.recent_confidences[-self.window_size:]
        
        # Calculate metrics
        if len(self.recent_predictions) >= 100:  # Minimum samples
            preds = torch.tensor(self.recent_predictions)
            labels = torch.tensor(self.recent_labels)
            confs = torch.tensor(self.recent_confidences)
            
            accuracy = (preds == labels).float().mean().item()
            avg_confidence = confs.mean().item()
            
            # Simple ECE calculation
            ece = abs(accuracy - avg_confidence)
            
            self.ece_history.append(ece)
            self.accuracy_history.append(accuracy)
            self.confidence_history.append(avg_confidence)
            self.timestamps.append(datetime.datetime.now())
    
    def detect_shift(self, threshold: float = 0.05) -> bool:
        """
        Detect if calibration has degraded significantly.
        
        Args:
            threshold: ECE threshold for triggering alert
            
        Returns:
            True if shift detected
        """
        if len(self.ece_history) < 10:
            return False
        
        recent_ece = np.mean(self.ece_history[-10:])
        baseline_ece = np.mean(self.ece_history[:10]) if len(self.ece_history) > 10 else recent_ece
        
        return recent_ece > baseline_ece + threshold
    
    def plot_monitoring(self, save_path: str = 'calibration_monitoring.png'):
        """Plot calibration metrics over time."""
        if len(self.ece_history) < 2:
            print("Not enough data to plot")
            return
        
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 10))
        
        x = range(len(self.ece_history))
        
        # ECE over time
        axes[0].plot(x, self.ece_history, 'b-', linewidth=2)
        axes[0].axhline(y=0.05, color='r', linestyle='--', label='Warning Threshold')
        axes[0].set_ylabel('ECE', fontsize=12)
        axes[0].set_title('Expected Calibration Error Over Time', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        axes[0].legend()
        axes[0].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Accuracy over time
        axes[1].plot(x, self.accuracy_history, 'g-', linewidth=2, label='Accuracy')
        axes[1].plot(x, self.confidence_history, 'orange', linewidth=2, label='Confidence')
        axes[1].set_ylabel('Value', fontsize=12)
        axes[1].set_title('Accuracy vs Confidence Over Time', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        axes[1].legend()
        axes[1].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        # Calibration gap
        gap = [abs(a - c) for a, c in zip(self.accuracy_history, self.confidence_history)]
        axes[2].plot(x, gap, 'r-', linewidth=2)
        axes[2].set_xlabel('Update Step', fontsize=12)
        axes[2].set_ylabel('Calibration Gap', fontsize=12)
        axes[2].set_title('Calibration Gap Over Time', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
        axes[2].grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close()
        print(f"Monitoring plot saved to '{save_path}'")
    
    def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """Get summary statistics."""
        if not self.ece_history:
            return {}
        
        return {
            'current_ece': self.ece_history[-1] if self.ece_history else 0,
            'mean_ece': np.mean(self.ece_history),
            'max_ece': np.max(self.ece_history),
            'current_accuracy': self.accuracy_history[-1] if self.accuracy_history else 0,
            'mean_accuracy': np.mean(self.accuracy_history),
            'shift_detected': self.detect_shift()
        }

def credit_scoring_fairness_example():
    """
    Case Study: Fair Credit Scoring with Multi-Calibration
    
    Demonstrates how multi-calibration ensures fairness across demographic
    groups in financial applications.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("CASE STUDY: FAIR CREDIT SCORING")
    print("="*80)
    print("\nScenario: Credit risk assessment with fairness constraints")
    print("Classes: Low Risk, Medium Risk, High Risk")
    print("Protected Attributes: Gender, Age Group\n")
    
    # Simulate credit application data
    num_applications = 2000
    num_features = 30  # Financial features
    num_classes = 3  # Risk levels
    
    X, y = create_synthetic_dataset(
        num_samples=num_applications,
        num_features=num_features,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        noise_level=0.15
    )
    
    # Create demographic attributes
    gender = torch.randint(0, 2, (num_applications,))  # 0: Female, 1: Male
    age_group = torch.randint(0, 3, (num_applications,))  # 0: Young, 1: Middle, 2: Senior
    
    # Split data
    train_size = 1200
    val_size = 400
    
    X_train, y_train = X[:train_size], y[:train_size]
    X_val, y_val = X[train_size:train_size+val_size], y[train_size:train_size+val_size]
    X_test, y_test = X[train_size+val_size:], y[train_size+val_size:]
    
    gender_val = gender[train_size:train_size+val_size]
    age_group_val = age_group[train_size:train_size+val_size]
    
    gender_test = gender[train_size+val_size:]
    age_group_test = age_group[train_size+val_size:]
    
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    # Train base credit scoring model
    print("Training credit scoring model...")
    train_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_train, y_train), batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    credit_model = create_base_model(num_features=num_features, num_classes=num_classes, hidden_size=128)
    credit_model = train_base_model(credit_model, train_loader, num_epochs=40, device=device)
    
    # Apply multi-calibration for fairness
    print("\nApplying multi-calibration for fairness...")
    multi_cal = MultiCalibrator(
        base_model=credit_model,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        group_attributes=['gender', 'age_group'],
        num_groups_per_attribute=[2, 3]
    )
    multi_cal = multi_cal.to(device)
    
    # Calibrate per group
    print("\nCalibrating for each demographic group...")
    
    # Collect data per group
    group_data = defaultdict(lambda: {'inputs': [], 'labels': []})
    
    for i in range(len(X_val)):
        for attr, attr_val in [('gender', gender_val[i]), ('age_group', age_group_val[i])]:
            key = f"{attr}_{attr_val.item()}"
            group_data[key]['inputs'].append(X_val[i].unsqueeze(0))
            group_data[key]['labels'].append(y_val[i].unsqueeze(0))
    
    # Calibrate each group
    with torch.no_grad():
        credit_model.eval()
        
        for attr_idx, attr in enumerate(['gender', 'age_group']):
            num_groups = [2, 3][attr_idx]
            
            for group_id in range(num_groups):
                key = f"{attr}_{group_id}"
                
                if key in group_data and group_data[key]['inputs']:
                    inputs = torch.cat(group_data[key]['inputs']).to(device)
                    labels = torch.cat(group_data[key]['labels']).to(device)
                    
                    logits = credit_model(inputs)
                    calibrator = multi_cal.group_calibrators[attr][group_id]
                    calibrator.fit(logits, labels, max_iter=50)
    
    # Evaluate fairness on test set
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("FAIRNESS EVALUATION")
    print("-"*60)
    
    risk_levels = ['Low Risk', 'Medium Risk', 'High Risk']
    gender_names = ['Female', 'Male']
    age_names = ['Young', 'Middle-Aged', 'Senior']
    
    # Analyze calibration by group
    with torch.no_grad():
        X_test_device = X_test.to(device)
        
        print("\nCalibration by Gender:")
        for g_id in range(2):
            mask = gender_test == g_id
            if mask.sum() > 0:
                group_inputs = X_test_device[mask]
                group_labels = y_test[mask].to(device)
                
                group_info = {'gender': torch.full((len(group_inputs),), g_id)}
                logits = multi_cal(group_inputs, group_info)
                probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
                
                preds = probs.argmax(dim=-1)
                accuracy = (preds == group_labels).float().mean()
                confidence = probs.max(dim=-1)[0].mean()
                
                print(f"  {gender_names[g_id]}:")
                print(f"    Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
                print(f"    Avg Confidence: {confidence:.4f}")
                print(f"    Calibration Gap: {abs(accuracy-confidence):.4f}")
        
        print("\nCalibration by Age Group:")
        for a_id in range(3):
            mask = age_group_test == a_id
            if mask.sum() > 0:
                group_inputs = X_test_device[mask]
                group_labels = y_test[mask].to(device)
                
                group_info = {'age_group': torch.full((len(group_inputs),), a_id)}
                logits = multi_cal(group_inputs, group_info)
                probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
                
                preds = probs.argmax(dim=-1)
                accuracy = (preds == group_labels).float().mean()
                confidence = probs.max(dim=-1)[0].mean()
                
                print(f"  {age_names[a_id]}:")
                print(f"    Accuracy: {accuracy:.4f}")
                print(f"    Avg Confidence: {confidence:.4f}")
                print(f"    Calibration Gap: {abs(accuracy-confidence):.4f}")
    
    # Example predictions
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("EXAMPLE CREDIT DECISIONS")
    print("-"*60)
    
    for i in range(5):
        X_sample = X_test[i:i+1].to(device)
        true_risk = risk_levels[y_test[i].item()]
        applicant_gender = gender_names[gender_test[i].item()]
        applicant_age = age_names[age_group_test[i].item()]
        
        group_info = {
            'gender': gender_test[i:i+1],
            'age_group': age_group_test[i:i+1]
        }
        
        logits = multi_cal(X_sample, group_info)
        probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
        pred_risk = risk_levels[probs.argmax(dim=-1).item()]
        confidence = probs.max(dim=-1)[0].item()
        
        print(f"\nApplicant {i+1}:")
        print(f"  Demographics: {applicant_gender}, {applicant_age}")
        print(f"  True Risk: {true_risk}")
        print(f"  Predicted Risk: {pred_risk} (confidence: {confidence:.2%})")
        print(f"  Risk Probabilities: Low={probs[0,0]:.2%}, "
              f"Medium={probs[0,1]:.2%}, High={probs[0,2]:.2%}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("Key Insights:")
    print("  • Multi-calibration ensures fair confidence scores across groups")
    print("  • Prevents systematic over/under-confidence for protected groups")
    print("  • Enables compliant and ethical lending decisions")
    print("  • Maintains accuracy while improving fairness")
    print("="*80)


def ensemble_vs_single_model_study():
    """
    Comparative study: Ensemble Calibration vs Single Model Calibration
    
    Demonstrates the benefits of ensemble methods for uncertainty estimation.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPARATIVE STUDY: ENSEMBLE VS SINGLE MODEL")
    print("="*80)
    print("\nComparing uncertainty quality between approaches\n")
    
    # Create challenging dataset with noise
    num_samples = 2000
    num_features = 20
    num_classes = 5
    
    X, y = create_synthetic_dataset(
        num_samples=num_samples,
        num_features=num_features,
        num_classes=num_classes,
        noise_level=0.25

        noise_level=0.25  # High noise to make uncertainty estimation challenging
    )
    
    # Split data
    train_size = 1200
    cal_size = 400
    
    X_train, y_train = X[:train_size], y[:train_size]
    X_cal, y_cal = X[train_size:train_size+cal_size], y[train_size:train_size+cal_size]
    X_test, y_test = X[train_size+cal_size:], y[train_size+cal_size:]
    
    device = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'
    
    # Create data loaders
    train_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_train, y_train), batch_size=32, shuffle=True)
    cal_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_cal, y_cal), batch_size=32)
    test_loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X_test, y_test), batch_size=32)
    
    results_comparison = {}
    
    # ========================================================================
    # APPROACH 1: Single Model with Temperature Scaling
    # ========================================================================
    print("="*60)
    print("APPROACH 1: Single Model with Temperature Scaling")
    print("="*60)
    
    print("\nTraining single model...")
    single_model = create_base_model(num_features, num_classes)
    single_model = train_base_model(single_model, train_loader, num_epochs=40, device=device)
    
    # Apply temperature scaling
    temp_scaler = TemperatureScaling(num_classes)
    temp_scaler.to(device)
    
    all_logits = []
    all_labels = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        single_model.eval()
        for inputs, labels in cal_loader:
            inputs = inputs.to(device)
            logits = single_model(inputs)
            all_logits.append(logits)
            all_labels.append(labels.to(device))
    
    all_logits = torch.cat(all_logits)
    all_labels = torch.cat(all_labels)
    temp_scaler.fit(all_logits, all_labels)
    
    # Evaluate on test set
    print("\nEvaluating single model...")
    all_probs_single = []
    all_labels_test = []
    all_correct_single = []
    
    with torch.no_grad():
        for inputs, labels in test_loader:
            inputs, labels = inputs.to(device), labels.to(device)
            logits = single_model(inputs)
            calibrated_logits = temp_scaler(logits)
            probs = F.softmax(calibrated_logits, dim=-1)
            
            preds = probs.argmax(dim=-1)
            correct = (preds == labels)
            
            all_probs_single.append(probs.cpu())
            all_labels_test.append(labels.cpu())
            all_correct_single.append(correct.cpu())
    
    all_probs_single = torch.cat(all_probs_single)
    all_labels_test = torch.cat(all_labels_test)
    all_correct_single = torch.cat(all_correct_single)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    accuracy_single = all_correct_single.float().mean()
    ece_single = calculate_ece(all_probs_single, all_labels_test)
    
    # Uncertainty analysis
    confidences_single = all_probs_single.max(dim=-1)[0]
    uncertainty_single = 1 - confidences_single
    
    # Separate correct and incorrect predictions
    uncertainty_correct_single = uncertainty_single[all_correct_single].mean()
    uncertainty_incorrect_single = uncertainty_single[~all_correct_single].mean()
    
    results_comparison['single_model'] = {
        'accuracy': accuracy_single.item(),
        'ece': ece_single.item(),
        'uncertainty_correct': uncertainty_correct_single.item(),
        'uncertainty_incorrect': uncertainty_incorrect_single.item(),
        'uncertainty_gap': (uncertainty_incorrect_single - uncertainty_correct_single).item()
    }
    
    print(f"\nSingle Model Results:")
    print(f"  Accuracy: {accuracy_single:.4f}")
    print(f"  ECE: {ece_single:.4f}")

    print(f"  Avg Uncertainty (Incorrect): {uncertainty_incorrect_single:.4f}")

    all_mutual_info = torch.cat(all_mutual_info)
    all_pred_entropy = torch.cat(all_pred_entropy)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    accuracy_ensemble = all_correct_ensemble.float().mean()

    uncertainty_ensemble = 1 - confidences_ensemble
    
    uncertainty_correct_ensemble = uncertainty_ensemble[all_correct_ensemble].mean()
    uncertainty_incorrect_ensemble = uncertainty_ensemble[~all_correct_ensemble].mean()

def create_reliability_diagram_comparison(
    models_dict: Dict[str, Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
    save_path: str = 'reliability_diagrams.png',
    n_bins: int = 10
):
    """
    Create reliability diagrams for multiple models side-by-side.
    
    Args:
        models_dict: Dictionary mapping model names to (probs, labels) tuples
        save_path: Path to save the figure
        n_bins: Number of bins for calibration
    """
    num_models = len(models_dict)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, num_models, figsize=(6*num_models, 5))
    
    if num_models == 1:
        axes = [axes]
    
    for idx, (model_name, (probs, labels)) in enumerate(models_dict.items()):
        ax = axes[idx]
        
        # Calculate binned statistics
        confidences, predictions = probs.max(dim=1)
        accuracies = predictions.eq(labels)
        
        bin_boundaries = np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins + 1)
        bin_lowers = bin_boundaries[:-1]
        bin_uppers = bin_boundaries[1:]
        
        bin_accs = []
        bin_confs = []
        bin_counts = []
        
        for bin_lower, bin_upper in zip(bin_lowers, bin_uppers):
            in_bin = (confidences > bin_lower) & (confidences <= bin_upper)
            prop_in_bin = in_bin.float().mean()
            
            if prop_in_bin > 0:
                accuracy_in_bin = accuracies[in_bin].float().mean()
                avg_confidence_in_bin = confidences[in_bin].mean()
                bin_accs.append(accuracy_in_bin.item())
                bin_confs.append(avg_confidence_in_bin.item())
                bin_counts.append(in_bin.sum().item())
            else:
                bin_accs.append(0)
                bin_confs.append((bin_lower + bin_upper) / 2)
                bin_counts.append(0)
        
        # Plot
        ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--', linewidth=2, label='Perfect Calibration')
        
        # Bar plot
        bin_width = 1.0 / n_bins
        colors = ['green' if abs(acc - conf) < 0.1 else 'orange' if abs(acc - conf) < 0.2 else 'red'
                 for acc, conf in zip(bin_accs, bin_confs)]
        
        ax.bar(bin_confs, bin_accs, width=bin_width*0.8, alpha=0.6, 
               edgecolor='black', color=colors)
        
        # Add sample counts as text
        for conf, acc, count in zip(bin_confs, bin_accs, bin_counts):
            if count > 0:
                ax.text(conf, acc, str(count), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8)
        
        # Calculate ECE
        ece = sum(abs(acc - conf) * count for acc, conf, count in zip(bin_accs, bin_confs, bin_counts))
        ece /= sum(bin_counts)
        
        ax.set_xlabel('Confidence', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_ylabel('Accuracy', fontsize=12)
        ax.set_title(f'{model_name}\nECE: {ece:.4f}', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold')
        ax.legend(fontsize=10)
        ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
        ax.set_xlim([0, 1])
        ax.set_ylim([0, 1])
        ax.set_aspect('equal')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print(f"Reliability diagrams saved to '{save_path}'")


def visualize_prediction_uncertainty_2d(
    model: nn.Module,
    X: torch.Tensor,
    y: torch.Tensor,
    uncertainty_measure: str = 'entropy',
    save_path: str = 'uncertainty_2d.png'
):
    """
    Visualize predictions and uncertainty in 2D using PCA.
    
    Args:
        model: Calibrated model
        X: Input features
        y: True labels
        uncertainty_measure: 'entropy', 'confidence', or 'mutual_info'
        save_path: Path to save figure
    """
    from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
    
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    
    # Project to 2D using PCA
    pca = PCA(n_components=2)
    X_2d = pca.fit_transform(X.cpu().numpy())
    
    # Get predictions and uncertainty
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        X_device = X.to(device)
        
        if isinstance(model, EnsembleCalibratedModel):
            logits = model(X_device)
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            uncertainty_metrics = model.get_uncertainty_metrics(X_device)
            
            if uncertainty_measure == 'entropy':
                uncertainty = uncertainty_metrics['predictive_entropy'].cpu().numpy()
            elif uncertainty_measure == 'mutual_info':
                uncertainty = uncertainty_metrics['mutual_information'].cpu().numpy()
            else:
                uncertainty = 1 - uncertainty_metrics['confidence'].cpu().numpy()
        else:
            logits = model(X_device)
            probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
            
            if uncertainty_measure == 'entropy':
                uncertainty = -torch.sum(probs * torch.log(probs + 1e-10), dim=-1).cpu().numpy()
            else:
                uncertainty = 1 - probs.max(dim=-1)[0].cpu().numpy()
        
        predictions = probs.argmax(dim=-1).cpu().numpy()
    
    # Create visualization
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))
    
    # Plot 1: Predictions
    ax = axes[0]
    scatter = ax.scatter(X_2d[:, 0], X_2d[:, 1], c=predictions, 
                        cmap='tab10', alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('PC1', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel('PC2', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_title('Predictions in 2D Space', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax, label='Predicted Class')
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    # Plot 2: Uncertainty
    ax = axes[1]
    scatter = ax.scatter(X_2d[:, 0], X_2d[:, 1], c=uncertainty, 
                        cmap='YlOrRd', alpha=0.6, s=50, edgecolors='black', linewidth=0.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('PC1', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_ylabel('PC2', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_title(f'Uncertainty ({uncertainty_measure}) in 2D Space', 
                fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
    plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax, label='Uncertainty')
    ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close()
    print(f"2D uncertainty visualization saved to '{save_path}'")
